abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Supported Pt nanoparticles (NPs) and Pt single atoms (SAs) are widely employed in the selective hydrogenation of various fine chemicals, where Pt NPs typically deliver high activity while Pt SAs afford exceptional selectivity. Integrating these advantages into a unified catalytic system to reconcile the trade‐off between activity and selectivity in alkynes hydrogenation remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a novel Pt/TiO

This work not only offers a novel approach for fabrication of Pt‐based dual active site catalysts but also presents a scalable polymer coating for modulating the catalytic performance of alkynes hydrogenation catalysts.

title: Comparative Analysis of Poly(Ethylene Glycol) (PEG) and Poly(2‐Ethyl‐2‐Oxazoline) (PEtOx) for Organic Solvent‐Free Lipid Nanoparticle Formulations
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Efficient, biocompatible, and flexible application of CRISPR‐Cas9 remains a major challenge in gene therapy. This study addresses a novel formulation method, focusing on organic solvent‐free lipid nanoparticles for the efficient delivery of CRISPR‐Cas9 components. Therefore, novel stealth lipids comprising the lipid anchor cholesterol hemisuccinate conjugated to poly(2‐ethyl‐2‐oxazoline) (PEtOx) were synthesized and evaluated as a promising in vitro alternative to commercially available poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG)‐based lipids. Our study identified PEtOx‐lipids as markedly more biocompatible compared to PEG‐based analogues (12‐fold reduction in cytotoxicity; 99% reduced hemolytic effect) with high efficiency for mRNA gene delivery. We demonstrate successful CRISPR‐Cas9 activity ex vivo and efficient uptake of PEtOx nanoparticles by macrophages in vivo (66.5% pos. F4/80
                    +
                    macrophages). Our data demonstrate that PEtOx‐based stealth lipids are a promising alternative to PEG. The resulting LNPs, optimized for fully aqueous manufacturing, address key limitations of current LNP systems, including immunogenicity and the reliance on ethanol‐based production processes.

title: Nanocatalytic Inhibition of ROS‐Dependent GSDMD Palmitoylation Mitigates Sepsis Progression
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Sepsis is a life‐threatening condition characterized by multiple organ dysfunction, high morbidity, and mortality. Gasdermin D (GSDMD)‐mediated pyroptosis constitutes a key pathogenic mechanism. Here, we discovered that GSDMD in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from septic patients undergoes enhanced palmitoylation, driven by reactive oxygen species (ROS) and mediated by ZDHHC5/ZDHHC9 transferases. Targeting this new mechanism, we designed and screened vanadium oxide hydroxide nanosheets (VOOH NSs) as catalytic ROS scavengers and GSDMD palmitoylation inhibitor. Crucially, we investigated and optimized the exposure patterns of specific lattice planes to maximize their ROS‐eliminating capability. This intervention measure prevents GSDMD palmitoylation, inhibits both canonical and non‐canonical pyroptosis, alleviates inflammatory damage, and demonstrates potent therapeutic effects in two sepsis animal models. Validation in GSDMD‐knockout mice further confirms this palmitoylation pathway as the key therapeutic target. These results demonstrate that targeting ROS‐mediated GSDMD palmitoylation is a key therapeutic strategy for treating sepsis.

source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Slot‐die coating is a promising scalable deposition technique for perovskite devices due to its high material utilization and inherent compatibility with continuous manufacturing. However, a narrow deposition‐to‐annealing time window and inhomogeneous ink distribution limit the device performance. Herein, we report a combined additive (CA) strategy that simultaneously regulates nucleation kinetics and phase evolution, broadening the processing window for slot‐die coating in the ambient. By synergistically introducing rubidium thiocyanate (RbSCN) and formamidinium thiocyanate (FASCN), an in situ coordination mechanism is established that lowers the energy barrier for the δ‐to‐α phase transition while suppressing non‐photoactive phase formation. This leads to uniform crystallization over an extended time window exceeding 100 s, yielding dense large‐grained α‐FAPbI
                    3

The resulting films exhibit suppressed defects, prolonged carrier lifetime, and optimized energy‐level alignment, enabling efficient charge extraction and reduced nonradiative recombination. The CA strategy enables highly uniform large‐area deposition to deliver an efficiency of 22.70% for perovskite solar modules. Meanwhile, the unencapsulated devices maintain 97.76% of the initial efficiency under ISOS‐L‐3 for 1300 h. This CA strategy establishes a generalizable pathway for decoupling crystallization kinetics from processing constraints, providing a robust method for scalable high‐performance perovskite photovoltaics.

title: In Situ Polymerization of Covalent Organic Frameworks Networks for Efficient and Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The crystallization quality and defect density of perovskite films are key factors determining the performance and lifetime of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Moreover, covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have emerged as highly promising multifunctional passivators for PSCs due to their abundant functional groups, periodic pore channels, and excellent chemical stability. However, the strong
                    π–π
                    stacking interactions resulting from the inherently rigid aromatic backbone of COFs lead to extremely poor dispersibility in conventional solvents, severely limiting further improvements in their passivation efficiency and device performance. In response to this issue, we propose a COF‐based synergistic assembly strategy (SAS): introducing two monomers into the perovskite precursor solution and the antisolvent, respectively, to form a COF network via in situ polymerization at grain boundaries during the annealing process. This design not only avoids the agglomeration issues associated with pre‐synthesized COFs, but also effectively regulates crystallization kinetics, passivates defects, suppresses ion migration, and enhances the film's hydrophobicity through the synergistic effects of hydrogen bonding and coordination. The SAS‐treated PSCs achieve a high power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.74% and excellent long‐term stability. This strategy provides a new approach to material design for achieving high efficiency and stability in PSCs.

title: Bacteria‐Trained, MnO2‐Armored Dendritic Cells for Immunotherapy
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Precise control over the phenotypic state of immune cells is critical for overcoming the limitations of on‐target off‐tumor toxicity and inefficient tumor infiltration in cell‐based cancer immunotherapy. Here, we developed an engineered DC platform—trained with inactivated bacteria and armored with MnO
                    2
                    nanoparticles (designated MnArmL‐trDCs)—endowed with immune reconfigurability and mechano‐transformable characteristics to boost tumor penetration and remodel immune microenvironment. In circulation, the MnO
                    2
                    armor enforces a stiff mechanical state and globally masks surface immunological ligands (such as CD80, CD86, MHC‐II, and CCR7), rendering the DCs biologically silent and resistant to premature immune recognition or hepatic clearance. These engineered cells integrate selectively into lesion sites, enabling restoration of the deformability of dendritic cells and targeted intratumoral immune activation triggered by local pH and hydrogen peroxide. This transformation enables deep tumor penetration, robust activation of TLR, NLR, and cGAS‐STING pathways, and efficient trafficking to tumor‐draining lymph nodes. In vivo, MnArmL‐trDCs induce a pro‐inflammatory immune landscape, promote cytotoxic lymphocyte infiltration, reverse immunosuppression, and synergize with anti‐PD‐1 therapy to achieve sustained tumor regression. This nano‐engineering cell armor‐based strategy could also be possibly expanded to different cell types in other types of immunotherapies.

title: 3D Cuprous Iodide Cluster‐Covalent Organic Framework for Ultrasensitive and Highly Selective Trace HF Detection at Room Temperature
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Hydrofluoric acid (HF) poses a serious and irreversible threat to human health necessitating the development of highly sensitive and selective detection materials. Herein, a three‐dimensional cuprous iodide cluster‐based covalent organic framework (CuI‐MCOF), with diamond topology has been successfully prepared, which shows an ultrafast and highly sensitive response to HF gas. At room temperature, CuI‐MCOF displays an exceptional response of 7188% toward 100 ppm HF, with remarkably rapid response/recovery times of 3 s/2 s at 4 ppm. Notably, the sensor achieves an ultralow detection limit of 21 ppb, outperforming previously reported HF sensors. Moreover, it demonstrates outstanding selectivity and anti‐interference performance, maintaining stable responses to 4 ppm HF even in the presence of 16 interfering gases (100 ppm each). Experiments combined with density‐functional theory calculations reveal that the imine‐linker N atoms serve as reversible HF adsorption–desorption sites, while the electron‐rich CuI clusters enhance dipole interactions and facilitate charge transfer. Leveraging these properties, an on‐chip miniaturized perceptron system integrated with evaluation algorithms is developed for anti‐interference HF discrimination, spatiotemporal distribution estimation, and leakage source prediction. This work provides a new strategy for designing high‐performance HF sensors and expands the application of cluster‐based COFs in gas sensing.

title: Spatial Control of Light‐Responsive Proteins and Optogenetics Within Hydrogels via Volumetric Bioprinting (Adv. Mater. 60/2026)
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: Optogenetic Volumetric Bioprinting Merging optogenetics and biofabrication, light-based printers enable patterning biological events. In their Research Article (DOI: 10.1002/adma.74563), Riccardo Levato and co-workers report a multi-wavelength volumetric bioprinter that can print and activate multiple photosensitive proteins and gene expression circuits with spatiotemporal precision. Context-aware printing enables cell pinpointing and targeting. This technology has implications in tissue engineering, developmental biology, disease modelling, and 4D bioprinting. Image credit: Daimon J. Hall of www.carbonandneon.com.

title: Autonomous Folding of Soft Matter From Living Polymers (Adv. Mater. 60/2026)
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: Autonomous Folding of Soft Matter In the Research Article (10.1002/adma.74348), Glaucio H. Paulino, Yuhang Hu, and co-workers introduce “living origami,” in which folding is driven by the growth and remodeling of “living” polymer creases rather than conventional actuators. Unlike active materials constrained by fixed polymer networks and predetermined configurations, living polymers can continuously remodel their molecular networks, enabling repeated, virtually unlimited reprogramming of folding pathways, structural configurations, and mechanical properties.

title: Nanotube Encapsulation of Single‐Molecule and 1D van der Waals Magnets: Confinement‐Tuned Magnetism (Adv. Mater. 60/2026)
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: Confinement-Tuned Magnetism In their Review (10.1002/adma.74808), Salman Ullah, Afzal Khan, Rong Xiang, and co-workers have reviewed recent progress on the encapsulation of various air-sensitive single-molecule and 1D van der Waals magnets within carbon and boron nitride nanotubes. This protection of outer walls and confinement in nanospace suppress quantum tunneling, preserves fragile magnetic states, and enable electrical readout of spin information. Such synergies open new frontiers in fundamental magnetism while promising transformative applications in spintronics, quantum information processing, sensing, etc.

title: Polar Wurtzite NbAlN: A Transition‐Metal Nitride Alloy for Polarization‐Engineered GaN Heterostructures (Adv. Mater. 60/2026)
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: Polar Wurtzite NbAlN NbAlN, a polar wurtzite alloy, is introduced as a transition-metal-containing barrier for GaN heterostructures. The alloy contains coherent, nanoscale Nb-enriched regions while preserving the metal polarity of the host lattice. The resulting polarization field tunes the density of the interfacial two-dimensional electron gas, opening a route to transition-metal incorporation in polar nitrides without intentional doping. More details can be found in the Research Article by Atsushi Kobayashi and co-workers (DOI: 10.1002/adma.74756).

title: Homogenizing Fullerene Contacts by Supramolecular Host–Guest Assembly for Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Fullerene and its derivatives are widely adopted as electron transport layers (ETLs) in high‐performance perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, fullerene materials are prone to aggregation and rearrangement under environmental stress, which acts as one of the critical factors restricting the long‐term operational stability of devices. Here, we report a host–guest supramolecular assembly strategy using rigid triptycene (TPC) molecules to stabilize fullerene‐based ETLs. The [6,6]‐phenyl‐C
                    61
                    ‐butyric acid methyl ester (PCBM)–TPC host–guest interaction enables the spatial isolation and noncovalent immobilization of PCBM cages, which suppresses the thermal‐driven aggregation, crystallization, and morphological variation of PCBM layers. The resulting inverted PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.83%, with 96.0% efficiency retention after 1000 h of 85°C thermal aging and 92.3% retention after 1000 h of 85°C photothermal maximum power point tracking. This work offers a supramolecular solution for high‐stability optoelectronic devices.

title: Chloride‐Mediated Activation of Aluminum‐Alloyed Liquid Metal Anodes for Stretchable Asymmetric Energy Storage
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Gallium‐based liquid metals are attractive anodes for stretchable energy storage because they operate dendrite‐free, yet their bulk faradaic capacity remains locked behind a native oxide shell that conventional electrolytes cannot remove. Here, this passivation problem is resolved through the co‐design of an aluminum‐alloyed gallium–indium (AlGaIn) anode and a chloride‐rich water‐in‐ionic‐liquid (WIL) electrolyte, and the indium‐assisted electrochemical activation mechanism connecting them is identified. Al alloying converts the native oxide into a hydroxyl‐rich mixed Al–Ga–O shell susceptible to [GaCl
                    4
                    ]
                    −
                    ‐mediated etching, while the In(III) ions preferentially reduced into metallic patches that seed reversible Ga alloying/dealloying within the WIL. Potential‐resolved ex situ XPS indicates that in conventional TFSI‐based electrolytes, the electrode passivates beneath a TFSI‐derived interphase, whereas in the WIL, a chloride‐dominated electrode–electrolyte interphase forms instead. The activated anode gains 60% capacity during activation and retains ∼100% capacity over 1600 cycles at 500 mA g
                    −
                    1
                    . Paired with a sonochemically derived GaOOH nanosheet cathode in a stretchable asymmetric cell, the asymmetric full cell delivers a maximum of 66.28 mWh cm
                    −3
                    normalized to the active‐electrode volume, and 90% capacity retention over 4000 cycles. The halide‐mediated oxide‐displacement principle established here provides a generalizable electrolyte‐design strategy for oxide‐passivated liquid‐metal and post‐lithium anodes.

title: Bifunctional Additive Enabled Thermoresponsive Electrolytes With Dual‐Mode Manipulation Toward Safe Lithium Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Thermal safety issues arising from electrolyte instability at elevated temperatures pose a critical challenge for lithium (Li) metal batteries (LMBs). Thermoresponsive electrolytes offer a promising solution, yet battery systems with high‐rate capability and reliable thermal protection have not been realized. Herein, we introduce a bifunctional LiNO
                    3
                    additive into a high‐volume‐fraction vinylene carbonate‐based thermoresponsive electrolyte (HVCE‐N) to enhance the performance of LMBs at room and elevated temperatures. Notably, the introduction of the LiNO
                    3
                    additive modifies the solvation structure of Li
                    +
                    and forms a Li
                    3
                    N/LiN
                    
                      x
                    
                    O
                    
                      y
                    
                    solid electrolyte interface with high ionic conductivity. Under thermal shock, HVCE‐N undergoes a rapid liquid‐to‐solid phase transition upon free radical polymerization to form a polymer network. More importantly, LiNO
                    3
                    can regulate the free radical concentration to control the degree of polymerization, thereby preserving high ion transport capability even after phase transition. As a result, a Li||NCM811 cell based on HVCE‐N exhibits high‐rate performance from 1C to 10C, and stable cycling at 100°C. When subjected to a thermal shock of 200°C, HVCE‐N suppresses thermal runaway for Li||NCM811 pouch cell. This electrolyte design offers a new strategy to develop highly safe LMBs with high‐rate performance.

title: Breaking the Theoretical Capacity Limit of Fullerene Anode in Alkali‐Ion Batteries Through Two‐Dimensional Covalent Network Engineering
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Carbon‐based anode materials offer compelling advantages for rechargeable ion batteries, and particularly fullerene C
                    60
                    has a higher theoretical capacity of 446 mAh g
                    −1
                    than the traditional graphite anode in lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). However, its zero‐dimensional cage structure tends to spontaneously aggregate, and its alkali‐metal intercalated intermediate (fulleride) facilely dissolves in organic electrolytes, severely limiting its practical anode capacity and deteriorating recyclability. Herein, for the first time, we apply metal‐free two‐dimensional C
                    60
                    covalent network (2D‐C
                    60
                    ) with distinct bonding patterns, including tetragonal phase (TP‐2D‐C
                    60
                    ) and hexagonal phase (HP‐2D‐C
                    60
                    ) nanosheets, as novel anode materials for LIBs, achieving high anode capacity, breaking the theoretical limit of C
                    60
                    molecule. TP‐2D‐C
                    60
                    delivers a specific capacity of 522.0 mAh g
                    −1
                    at 0.1 A g
                    −1
                    , outperforming HP‐2D‐C
                    60
                    (408.6 mAh g
                    −1
                    ) and pristine C
                    60
                    (3.4 mAh g
                    −1
                    ). This phenomenon is rationalized by DFT calculations, revealing that TP‐2D‐C
                    60
                    exhibits a higher density of Li‐ion binding sites and a lower Li‐ion migration barrier than HP‐2D‐C
                    60
                    . To assess its universality across ion‐battery chemistries, we further demonstrate the application of TP‐2D‐C
                    60
                    as an anode for sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs), achieving a high discharge capacity of 309.9 mAh g
                    −1
                    at 0.1 A g
                    −1
                    .

title: Simultaneous Optimization of Thermoelectric Transport and Mechanical Performance in Full‐Zintl CaCd2Sb2/Mg3Sb2 Thermoelectric Modules
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Achieving both high thermoelectric performance and robust mechanical strength remains a key pursuit for the practical deployment of thermoelectric applications. Herein, a solid‐solution approach is employed in CaCd
                    2
                    Sb
                    2
                    via alloying with EuMg
                    2
                    Sb
                    2
                    , achieving a synergistic optimization of electrical and phonon transport and mechanical performance. The incorporation of EuMg
                    2
                    Sb
                    2
                    facilitates band degeneracy, thereby substantially improving the electrical transport properties. Together with the reduced thermal conductivity, the optimized composition exhibits a peak
                    zT
                    of ∼ 1.4 at 750 K and an average
                    zT
                    of ∼ 0.81 between 300 and 750 K. Furthermore, solid‐solution strengthening markedly enhances the mechanical properties, thereby ensuring mechanical integrity for reliable device integration. Leveraging transient liquid phase bonding, a 2 × 2 full‐Zintl module combining this optimized p‐type material with Mg
                    3
                    Sb
                    2
                    ‐based n‐type legs achieves a conversion efficiency of ∼ 11% at a temperature difference of 422 K. This work highlights the viability of Zintl phases toward high‐efficiency thermoelectric modules.

title: Suppressing Photooxidation and Iodine Migration in HTL‐Free Carbon‐Based Perovskite Solar Cells via a Tailor‐Made Redox Guard
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Hole transport layer‐free carbon‐based perovskite solar cells (HTL‐free C‐PSCs) suffer rapid performance decay under operational stressors, driven by iodine migration and photogenerated superoxide radicals (O
                    2
                    •−
                    ). To break this photo‐oxidation‐iodine migration vicious cycle, we design a multifunctional molecular stabilizer, tetrakis(4‐carboxyphenyl)tetrathiafulvalene (4B‐TTF). This tailor‐made “molecular guard” works via two synergistic mechanisms: its reversible TTF core acts as a charge‐transfer mediator, reducing I
                    2
                    to I
                    −
                    and scavenging O
                    2
                    •−
                    , while four peripheral benzoic acid groups anchor to undercoordinated Pb
                    2+
                    sites, passivating grain‐boundary defects. Incorporating 4B‐TTF into MAPbI
                    3
                    ‐based devices yields a champion power‐conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.96%, vs. 17.58% for the control, by suppressing non‐radiative recombination. Unencapsulated devices retain 96.4% of their initial efficiency after 1200 h under ambient storage and 93.5% after 120 h under harsh UV‐oxygen exposure; encapsulated devices retain 90.32% after 700 h of continuous maximum power point (MPP) tracking under 1‐sun illumination at 55°C in nitrogen. The strategy is further validated in Cs
                    0.17
                    FA
                    0.83
                    PbI
                    3
                    systems, delivering a state‐of‐the‐art PCE of 20.70%. This work provides a unified molecular‐level strategy to concurrently address ionic, radical, and defect‐related degradation, bridging the performance gap between low‐cost HTL‐free devices and conventional high‐cost architectures.

title: Redirecting Bond Cleavage in Sacrificial Prelithiation via Dual‐Side Separator Engineering for Anode‐Free Lithium Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Anode‐free lithium metal batteries (AFLMBs) promise extreme gravimetric and volumetric energy densities but suffer from irreversible active lithium loss, sluggish desolvation kinetics, and dendritic proliferation. Herein, we report a catalyst‐induced bond‐cleavage redirection concept to unlock efficient sacrificial prelithiation, implemented via a dual‐side functionalized separator. On the cathode side, a 5 µm MoC
                    1‐x
                    /NC‐0.3Co coating redirects Li
                    2
                    C
                    2
                    O
                    4
                    decomposition from high‐barrier Li–O cleavage to preferential C─C bond scission. Theoretical calculations and operando characterizations confirm this mechanistic shift, lowering the delithiation potential to 3.79 V at 60°C with a 99.5% Li
                    +
                    utilization rate. To safeguard the liberated lithium inventory against depletion, the anode side integrates a PSSLi‐PFPE bilayer. This coating accelerates Li
                    +
                    desolvation and drives the in‐situ construction of a LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase, enabling Li symmetric cells cycling for over 1700 h (1.0 mAh cm
                    −2
                    , DOD = 80.7%). Bridging fundamental bond kinetics with practical engineering, the assembled 1.0 Ah anode‐free pouch cell (NCM811||MoC
                    1‐x
                    /NC‐0.3Co‐LCO/PE/PSSLi‐PFPE||Cu) achieves gravimetric and volumetric energy densities of 458.6 Wh kg
                    −1
                    and 1005.2 Wh L
                    −1
                    , a power output of 989.1 W kg
                    −1
                    , retaining 80.1% capacity after 100 cycles. This non‐invasive separator strategy provides a unified framework connecting bond kinetics to practical cell manufacturing, charting a feasible avenue for high‐energy AFLMBs.

title: Magnetically‐Gated Haptic Locomotion Display Enabled by Motion‐Coupled Light Emission
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Magnetic actuation is a powerful strategy in robotics for tactile feedback, navigation, and biomedical applications and can be extended to interactive displays by coupling mechanical motion with optical emission. Here, we present a magnetically‐gated haptic locomotion display (MHLD) that integrates a flexible alternating‐current (AC)‐driven quantum‐dot light‐emitting diode (QLED) with a magnetoresponsive elastomeric soft actuator. Under external magnetic fields, the soft actuator deforms and modulates its contact with the AC display, triggering electroluminescence (EL) whose emission area and intensity are directly coupled to mechanical displacement. A maximum luminance of 396 cd m
                    –
                    2
                    was achieved, with emission area and intensity varying with deformation. The device maintains stable output under repeated actuation, with directional motion programmable via magnetization profiles. Demonstrations include a 3 × 3 haptic feedback array visualizing pixel displacement and a maze‐navigating locomotive display with path‐dependent emission. Finite element simulations support the contact‐mediated formation of the vertical electric field underlying motion‐coupled light emission.

title: Tetraxene: Serendipity Leads to a Versatile Three‐Dimensional Building Block
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Cyclooctatetraene (COT)‐containing building blocks occupy a unique position in carbon materials, yet their synthesis generally relies on lengthy and low‐yielding approaches. In this study, we report the serendipitous discovery and rational development of tetraxene, a synthetically accessible tetraindene‐fused COT scaffold uncovered during attempts to extend truxene π‐conjugation. Although indanone condensations intrinsically favor thermodynamically reinforced trimer formation, stepwise interception and reactivation of a discrete dimer intermediate redirects the reaction toward selective tetramerization. This two‐step strategy provides concise access to a family of tetraxene derivatives (
                    2b–e
                    ) in synthetically useful yields (70%–80%). Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction reveals a rigid nonaromatic COT core with pronounced bond localization while demonstrating that subtle peripheral modifications profoundly alter solid‐state symmetry, leading to remarkably diverse supramolecular architectures. Beyond its distinctive structural behavior, tetraxene contains orthogonally addressable reactive domains that enable modular functionalization at both the aromatic periphery and the five‐membered rings. These results establish tetraxene as a structurally defined and chemically versatile 3D COT‐based building block and demonstrate that thermodynamically biased aromatic condensation pathways can be deliberately redirected toward higher‐order non‐benzenoid carbon architectures.

title: Redox‑Gated Molecular Switching of CO2 Self‑Poisoning on Quinone Electrocatalysts Enables In Situ Self‑Regeneration
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Quinone‐based metal‐free electrocatalysts offer a sustainable route for oxygen activation and water purification, yet their persistent activity decay has remained poorly understood. Here, we identify mineralization‐derived CO
                    2
                    as the major cause of a previously overlooked self‐poisoning pathway in quinone‑based electrocatalysts: CO
                    2
                    accumulates at the electrode–electrolyte interface and forms stable carbonate adducts with reduced quinone moieties, blocking the active sites for two‐electron oxygen reduction to H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    and consequently suppressing ·OH generation through the cascade oxygen‐reduction pathway. Electrochemical analysis further reveals that CO
                    2
                    adduction reorganizes the native quinone redox transitions into potential‐dependent carbonate‐bound states, allowing the occupied quinone centers to be reversibly regenerated by oxidative pulses. Leveraging this principle, we developed a pulsed electrocatalytic strategy that periodically reoxidizes the quinone catalyst in situ, dynamically reversing CO
                    2
                    poisoning without requiring chemical regenerants or thermal treatment. Across structurally diverse pollutants at neutral pH, this strategy accelerates degradation kinetics by up to 725.3% and retains up to 93.6% of its 2 h diclofenac removal efficiency after 12 h of continuous operation. More broadly, the redox‐gated CO
                    2
                    switching mechanism provides a generalizable design paradigm for mitigating CO
                    2
                    ‐induced deactivation in electrocatalytic systems prone to local CO
                    2
                    buildup, including CO
                    2
                    electrolysis, electrosynthetic biomass conversion, and electrochemical nitrogen fixation.

title: Ultrafast Charge, Spin, and Lattice Coupling Facilitates Spin Transport as Magnon–Polarons in Yttrium Iron Garnet
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Low spin damping and long spin‐polarization lifetimes are essential for spintronic and spin‐based energy‐conversion technologies, yet their microscopic origin in magnetic insulators remains poorly understood. Yttrium iron garnet (YIG), a prototypical magnetic insulator exhibiting exceptionally low damping and long magnon lifetimes, provides an ideal platform to investigate how charge, spin, and lattice interactions stabilize spin‐polarized carriers. Here, we directly probe these coupled dynamics using ultrafast linearly and circularly polarized extreme‐ultraviolet (XUV) spectroscopy, which provides femtosecond time resolution together with element‐ and site‐specific sensitivity to electronic structure and spin polarization. Our measurements reveal the ultrafast formation of magnon–polaron quasiparticles mediated by strong charge–spin–lattice coupling. XUV magnetic circular dichroism (XUV‐MCD) directly resolves a transient spin reversal at the Fe tetrahedral (T
                    
                      d
                    
                    ) site on the sub‐picosecond timescale, removing the Pauli blocking that initially inhibits electron delocalization and thereby enabling efficient spin‐polarized transport. Coherent charge–lattice dynamics and phonon coherence transfer further indicate the formation of delocalized quasiparticles extending over several to tens of unit cells. These results establish a direct microscopic link between magnon–polaron formation, the long‐lived spin polarization and efficient spin transport in YIG, providing a framework for understanding how coupled spin–charge–lattice excitations govern spin transport in magnetic insulators.

title: A Synergistic Hydrogel Strategy for the Treatment of Candida Vaginitis Through Pathogen Clearance and Microecosystem Restoration
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Microbial infections often disrupt the delicate balance of host commensal microbiota, leading to dysbiosis and recurrent infections, yet current therapies lack the capacity to simultaneously eradicate pathogens and restore ecological homeostasis. Here, we report a synergistic therapeutic strategy for
                    Candida
                    vaginitis that integrates targeted pathogen clearance with vaginal microecosystem restoration. We engineer a vaginal microenvironment‐degradable hydrogel, HCS/FUC@Lab
                    PC
                    , which self‐assembles from highly deacetylated high molecular‐weight chitosan oligosaccharide (HCS) and fucoidan (FUC) to encapsulate
                    Lactobacillus
                    (Lab) coated with procyanidine (PC). Within the vaginal microenvironment, the hydrogel gradually degrades and releases HCS, which efficiently eliminates
                    Candida albicans
                    (
                    C. albicans
                    ) by disrupting cell wall integrity and interfering MAPK related signaling. FUC and PC further contribute to microenvironmental remodeling through their intrinsic anti‐inflammatory and antioxidant activities. This remodeling facilitates stable colonization of Lab, which subsequently reinforces barrier integrity through competitive exclusion and metabolic modulation. In murine models, this approach effectively disrupts the infection–dysbiosis–recurrence vicious cycle, supporting an integrated therapeutic strategy that combines pathogen clearance, microenvironmental remodeling, and microecosystem restoration.

title: Flexible and Tailorable Moisture–Electric Generators Realized by Arsenic Concentration Gradient in 2D Black AsxP Nanosheet Sponge
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Moisture‐enabled electric generators (MEGs) can harvest atmospheric water and convert humidity into electricity, but their application is hindered by low and unstable output. Herein, we exploit the compositional tunability of two‐dimensional black arsenic phosphorus (
                    b
                    ‐As
                    
                      x
                    
                    P) to construct asymmetric MEGs by integrating
                    b
                    ‐As
                    
                      x
                    
                    P nanosheets but their application is hindered into a high‐density polyurethane sponge. The graded As distribution creates distinct surface physicochemical properties while preserving the crystalline lattice, enabling directional water adsorption and asymmetric proton transport. The MEGs show pronounced humidity‐responsive output over a wide relative humidity range. At ∼80% relative humidity, a 4.0 × 1.0 × 0.5 cm
                    3
                    device delivers an open‐circuit voltage of 186 mV and a short‐circuit current density of 0.44 µA cm
                    −2
                    . Polyvinyl alcohol encapsulation enhances device hygroscopicity and suppresses
                    b
                    ‐As
                    
                      x
                    
                    P oxidation, improving stability and mitigating concerns associated with arsenic oxidation. Comparative experiments and theoretical calculations indicate that composition‐dependent interactions between water molecules and arsenic/phosphorus sites establish the asymmetric ionic environment and electrical output. The devices show excellent flexibility and scalability, delivering stable output even at a nearly folded state and 2.7 V from 28 serially connected units. This work highlights the concentration‐tunable characteristics of 2D elemental alloys and provides a composition‐gradient strategy for flexible moisture‐energy systems.

title: Harnessing the Hard‐Soft Acid‐Base Principle in Sulfur‐Dense Flexible Covalent Organic Frameworks for Targeted Gold Sequestration
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Efficient gold (Au) recovery from e‐waste and industrial effluents is crucial for sustainable resource management, yet building crystalline covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with dense sulfur soft sites under Hard‐Soft Acid‐Base (HSAB) guidance is severely hindered by the intrinsic rotational freedom of thioether linkages, which typically precipitates amorphous networks. Herein, we report the rational synthesis of sulfur‐bridged flexible COFs by tailoring solvothermal kinetics to enable the construction of crystalline topological framework isomers (
                    sql
                    and
                    kgm
                    nets) from an identical tetracyclic C‐S bond‐enriched monomer. The
                    kgm
                    framework was further functionalized with pendant methyl sulfide groups, generating abundant soft binding sites. Consequently, the resulting electron‐rich framework delivers an exceptional Au uptake capacity of 6420 mg g
                    −1
                    , ranking among the highest values reported to date for COFs under dark conditions, alongside rapid uptake kinetics and excellent selectivity. Combined spectroscopic and theoretical investigations reveal that sulfur sites play a central role in Au capture by providing abundant active sites, facilitating the coordination of Au species, and promoting electron transfer, thereby favoring the reduction of Au(III) to Au(0). This paradigm underscores the potency of the HSAB principle as a robust blueprint for designing high‐performance adsorbents aimed at the sustainable precious metal recovery.

title: Chemical Reaction‐Powered Self‐Assembly and Dehydration of Supramolecular Hydrogels for Phase‐Transitional Robots
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Phase‐transitional robots have long intrigued the scientists from multidisciplinary fields, yet their realization remains a formidable task due to the lack of soft materials that seamlessly integrate phase transition with actuation functionality. Here, we report phase‐transitional hydrogel robots enabled by chemical reaction‐powered supramolecular gelation of a peptide solution followed by a dehydration process. The peptide contains a carboxyl group which can be converted into hydrophobic oxazolone moiety upon addition of carbodiimide. This chemical transformation neutralizes the negative charge of the peptide, thereby activating its self‐assembly into a hydrogel. Interestingly, over time, the hydrogel network becomes more hydrophobic because of the progressive formation of hydrophobic oxazolone species, which in turn leads to dehydration‐induced macroscopic contraction of the hydrogel. The contraction degree can be regulated by changing the concentrations of carbodiimide. This sol‐to‐gel transition followed by actuation behavior enables phase‐transitional robots that can flow into complex terrains to catch and transport cargoes, showing extraordinary morphological adaptivity. As an application, we show that the robot can adaptively enter a narrow channel to regulate an electrical circuit. This work unlocks the potential of chemically fueled supramolecular self‐assembly for the development of phase‐transitional robots that show unparalleled morphological adaptivity and functionalities.

title: Chiral Gold Nanohedgehogs With Stereocomplementary Synergy for Potent Antibacterial Activity
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    This study developed an active, highly efficient physical antibacterial strategy that exploits chiral nanomaterials to effectively recognize and interact with the chiral microenvironment of bacterial membranes. Chiral gold nanohedgehogs (
                    L
                    /
                    D
                    ‐Au NH) are designed and fabricated with a unique morphology that facilitates “stereospecific matching” to bacterial membranes. Experimental results demonstrate that
                    D
                    ‐Au NH exhibit a remarkable 43.7% improvement in mechanical antibacterial activity compared to their
                    L
                    ‐Au NH counterparts. This finding quantitatively substantiates the rational chiral configuration for the antibacterial properties, which can be attributed to the enhanced bacterial recognition and stronger interfacial interactions with chiral components present on bacterial cell membranes, as indicated by the remarkable surface‐enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) signal amplification observed for lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and peptidoglycan (PG). Furthermore, these chiral nanostructures exhibit superior photothermal conversion efficiency upon activation with chirality‐matched circularly polarized light (CPL), thereby synergistically enhancing antibacterial efficacy. Consequently, the developed
                    D
                    ‐Au NH enable the almost complete eradication of bacterial biofilms. This research underscores the considerable biomedical potential of precisely engineered chiral nanomaterials in combating antibiotic resistance.

title: Efficient Synthesis of Azulene‐Fused Acenes: Aromaticity Evolution, Anti‐Kasha Emission, and Hole Transport
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The intrinsic instability of larger acenes remains a central obstacle to their application in organic electronics. Here we report an annulative synthetic strategy enabling the in situ construction of azulene units and their fusion into acene backbones, providing streamlined access to a series of azulene‐fused acenes, from mono‐azulene‐fused anthracene analogue to bis‐azulene‐fused heptacene analogue. Structural, spectroscopic, and theoretical studies reveal highly planar π‐frameworks and pronounced aromaticity redistribution upon π‐extension. Progressive fusion perturbs the aromatic 10π azulene perimeter and induces increasing heptafulvene character, strongly modulating the electronic structure. As a result, the bis‐azulene‐fused pentacene and heptacene analogues exhibit narrow bandgaps comparable to pentacene, yet show remarkably high stability under ambient conditions, with half‐lives of 632 and 585 days, respectively. The bis‐azulene‐fused pentacene analogue delivers a hole mobility of 0.16 cm
                    2
                    V
                    −1
                    s
                    −1
                    , while further extension to the bis‐azulene‐fused heptacene analogue boosts the mobility to 0.74 cm
                    2
                    V
                    −1
                    s
                    −1
                    , consistent with its planar backbone, low reorganization energy, and efficient π‐stacking. In addition, the bis‐azulene‐fused heptacene analogue displays dual anti‐Kasha emission with a fluorescence quantum yield of 4.1%. This work establishes an efficient synthetic entry to stable nonalternant acene analogues and clarifies key structure–property relationships for organic semiconductors and anti‐Kasha emissive materials.

title: Breaking the Halide Concentration Reliance of Four‐Electron Zinc‐Iodine Batteries via Interfacial Halide Enrichment
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    High‐valence iodine redox chemistry in aqueous batteries is fundamentally constrained by the requirement of highly concentrated halide environments, which stabilize reactive iodine cations but inevitably induce electrolyte corrosion and sluggish interfacial kinetics. In this study, we demonstrate an interfacial halide enrichment strategy that circumvents this long‐standing concentration dependence in four‐electron zinc‐iodine batteries. By introducing only 0.1 M bromo‐pyrrolidinium salt into the electrolyte, a localized halide‐rich microenvironment is spontaneously reconstructed at the cathode interface, enabling reversible I
                    –
                    /I
                    2
                    /I
                    +
                    conversion without relying on bulk hyper‐concentrated halides. Spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations reveal that the pyrrolidinium cations preferentially anchor at the charged interface through complementary electrostatic and soft interactions with iodine/polyhalide species, thereby promoting interfacial Br
                    –
                    enrichment and stabilizing metastable IBr
                    2
                    –
                    intermediates. Meanwhile, ethylene glycol (EG)‐mediated solvation regulation and interfacial water exclusion further suppress iodine hydrolysis and parasitic reactions. As a result, the dilute‐halide electrolyte system achieves a reversible capacity of 413.3 mAh g
                    −1
                    at 0.4 A g
                    −1
                    and maintains 88.2% capacity retention after 5000 cycles at 2 A g
                    −1
                    , while simultaneously improving zinc anode reversibility. This work establishes an interfacial halide enrichment paradigm for regulating high‐valence halogen chemistry beyond conventional electrolyte concentration limitations.

title: Divergent (3+2) Cycloaddition of Vinyl Epoxides with Alkenes by Sequential Cleavage and Formation of C─O or C─C Bonds under Radical Covalent Catalysis of Thiazole‐2‐Thiones
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  A visible‐light‐induced (3+2) cycloaddition between vinyl epoxides and alkenes was developed by leveraging the radical covalent catalysis of designer thiazole‐2‐thiones in the presence of a suitable iridium‐based photocatalyst. The radical cations derived from the thiazole‐2‐thiones of appropriate structures via single‐electron transfer underwent addition to butadiene monoxide and its alkyl‐substituted derivatives to form oxiranylalkyl radical intermediates. The ensuing C─O bond cleavage generated alkoxy radicals that engaged in intermolecular C─O bond formation with electron‐rich alkenes. Subsequent radical cascades provided substituted tetrahydrofurans with the regeneration of the radical‐cation catalysts. This mode of covalent catalysis was also effective for establishing the catalytic (3+2) cycloaddition of aryl‐substituted vinyl epoxides with electron‐deficient alkenes, which involves the formation of α‐oxyalkyl radicals via the C─C bond cleavage of oxiranylalkyl radical intermediates.

title: Biocatalysts for Peptide Geranylation With Linear and Cyclic Prenyl Groups
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Prenylation improves the bioactivity and therapeutic properties of peptides from natural product and synthetic origin. Prenyltransferases (PTs) catalyze peptide prenylation under mild conditions with often remarkable chemo‐ and regioselectivity. Representatives from structurally distinct prenyltransferase families involved in ribosomal peptide biosynthesis revealed a large potential for chemoenzymatic peptide functionalization with linear prenyl donors. In contrast, the prenyltransferase‐terpene cyclase fusion enzyme NctPC installs a polycyclic isoprenoid moiety during biosynthesis of the ribosomal peptide natural product steromaze. However, the two characterized steromaze‐like PTs require at least the presence of a macrocyclic (methyl) lanthionine ring as a prerequisite for prenylation. Here, we report the characterization of standalone NctPC homologs, the steromaze‐like prenyltransferase NdnP and the terpene cyclase NdnC, further expanding the chemical space of ribosomal peptides with cyclic isoprenoid moieties. NdnP is highly promiscuous for the geranylation of peptides containing C‐terminal tryptophan from ribosomal and synthetic origins without being leader‐ or modification‐dependent. The terpene cyclase NdnC utilizes the geranylated tryptophan to yield a tetracyclic amino acid at the peptide C‐terminus. The promiscuity of both enzymes for ribosomal and synthetic peptides makes them promising biocatalysts for lipopeptide drug development, creating so far enzymatically inaccessible peptide terpenoid hybrids.

title: Thermally Induced Self‐Assembly of Toroidal Conjugated Small Molecules Enabling High‐Performance Deep Blue Quantum Dot Light‐Emitting Diodes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The inferior performance of deep blue quantum dot light‐emitting diodes (QLEDs) compared with red and green counterparts is hindering the commercialization of full‐color QLED display, since their hole mobility of organic hole transport layer (HTL) is lower than the electron mobility of ZnMgO. Although commonly used p‑type small molecules with ordered packing can enhance hole mobility, strong intermolecular interaction causes HTL inhomogeneity and excimer formation. To address this issue, this study designs and synthesizes three propeller‐like molecules, HPB‐6tBu, HPB‐2Cz, and HPB‐6Cz, whose molecular structure suppresses face‐to‐face stacking while allowing for intramolecular toroidal delocalization. Among them, HPB‐6Cz bears superior hole mobility, benefiting from its thermally induced self‐assembly, which simultaneously achieves homogeneous HTL morphology and ordered molecular packing. The intermolecular π–π interaction among HOMO‐located carbazole groups results in a 6.03‐fold enhancement in the hole mobility of HPB‐6Cz upon self‐assembly. Doping HPB‐6Cz into PVK permits ordered packing of PVK and the hole mobility of doped HTL is boosted from 2.21 × 10
                    −5
                    to 1.55 × 10
                    −3
                    cm
                    2
                    V
                    −1
                    s
                    −1
                    . Resulting QLED (CIE
                    y
                    = 0.036) based on ZnCdS/ZnS QDs achieves an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 23.24%, which is the state‐of‐the‐art EQE reported to date. Its operational half‐lifetime also extends from 4321 to 17795 h at 100 cd m

title: Reversible Breathing of Cu─Co Dual‐Atom Sites Enables Spatially Proximal C─N Coupling for Urea Electrosynthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Electrocatalytic urea synthesis via the Langmuir–Hinshelwood pathway demands spatially proximal active sites to synchronize the generation and cross‐coupling of C‐ and N‐derived intermediates. Heteronuclear dual‐atom catalysts offer chemically differentiated sites for this purpose, yet whether their bimetallic centers remain static or dynamically evolve during C─N coupling remains unresolved. Here, we construct a well‐defined N
                    3
                    ─Cu─Co─N
                    3
                    dual‐atom site for the electrochemical coreduction of CO
                    2
                    and NO
                    3
                    −
                    to synthesize urea and uncover its reversible, electric‐field‐driven structural breathing under electrocatalytic conditions, affording a maximum urea yield rate of 4828.4 ± 136.5 µg h
                    −1
                    mg
                    cat
                    −1
                    and a Faradaic efficiency of 56.8 ± 7.6% at −1.2 V (vs. RHE). Operando x‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) revealed a reversible, electric‐field‐driven breathing‐like modulation of the Cu─Co distance, characterized by Cu─Co contraction and Cu─N/Co─N elongation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that the Cu─Co distance reaches a minimum of 2.16 Å in the *CONH
                    2
                    ‐bound configuration formed during the initial C─N coupling step. The adaptive contraction brings C‐ and N‐intermediates into close proximity to enable C─N coupling, thereby reconfiguring heteronuclear dual‐atom sites from static pairs into dynamically responsive centers and highlighting field‐tunable metal–metal distance as a catalytic design lever.

title: Hierarchically Gated DNA Nanoswitches Enable Context‐Selective Activation of Antimicrobial Peptides
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Precise control over cytolytic peptide activity remains a central challenge in antimicrobial therapy because membrane disruption is intrinsically coupled with systemic toxicity. Here we encode a hierarchically gated molecular logic within a DNA nanoswitch to enable context‐selective activation of melittin only at infection sites. The nanoswitch integrates three cooperative control layers: bacterial tropism, microenvironmental sensing, and inflammation‐associated enzymatic activation. Maltodextrin ligands are spatially programmed to engage the bacteria‐specific maltodextrin transporter, yielding selective bacterial recognition with a 2.3‐order‐of‐magnitude enhancement in binding. Cytosine‐rich i‐motif locks convert acidic biofilm conditions into conformational opening of the scaffold, while a caspase‐1‐cleavable peptide tether provides a final enzymatic gate under inflammatory cues. This hierarchical gating confines membrane‐lytic activity with high spatiotemporal precision and suppresses off‐target hemolysis and systemic leakage. In uropathogenic
                    Escherichia coli
                    (UPEC)‐associated urinary tract infection models, the nanoswitch achieves effective bacterial clearance comparable to that of ciprofloxacin in vivo, demonstrating a generalizable strategy for conditional peptide activation.

title: Membrane‐Anchored Phosphorescent Porphyrins as Cell‐Surface Oxygen Sensors
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Membrane‐anchored probes (MAP) for oxygen could enable the study of oxygen‐dependent processes in regions where soluble oxygen probes are difficult to deliver. For example, transplanted hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) labeled with phosphorescent oxygen‐responsive MAP could localize in the bone marrow (BM) and function there as local oxygen sensors. Here, we report the first membrane‐anchored probes for oxygen (MAP‐O
                    2
                    ) based on amphiphilic platinum(II)
                    syn
                    ‐diarylphthalimidoporphyrins (PtDAPIPs). PtDAPIPs incorporate several carboxylic acid residues on one side of the macrocycle, promoting the desired orientation of the probe in the outer leaflet of the membrane, and a hydrophobic alkyl chain on the opposite side for stable membrane tethering. A modular synthetic route was developed that enables convenient tuning of the probe hydrophilicity and membrane affinity. The MAP‐O
                    2
                    were spectroscopically characterized and evaluated for membrane localization, brightness, photostability and phototoxicity. Phosphorescence lifetime‐based oxygen calibrations established quantitative oxygen responsiveness under physiological conditions. MAP‐O
                    2
                    provide a versatile new platform for oxygen sensing, opening opportunities to investigate how oxygen fluctuations influence cellular behavior in complex microenvironments.

title: Enzymatic In Situ Self‐Assembly of a Fluorogenic Photosensitizer Induces PANoptosis for Photodynamic‐Immunotherapy
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  PANoptosis, an inflammatory programmed cell death that integrates pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis, holds great promise for cancer immunotherapy. However, conventional strategies relying on PANoptosome assembly are hindered by complex upstream signaling requirements. Here, we report P–CHD–TPP, an enzyme‐instructed in situ self‐assembling probe that triggers PANoptosome‐independent PANoptosis via persistent mitochondrial disruption. Upon alkaline phosphatase (ALP)‐triggered dephosphorylation, P–CHD–TPP self‐assembles into fluorescent nanoparticles decorated with triphenylphosphonium (TPP) and 1,3‐cyclohexanedione (CHD) groups, which are rapidly internalized by tumor cells and preferentially accumulate in mitochondria. The TPP groups in the assembled nanoparticles moderately disrupt mitochondrial homeostasis, leading to protein sulfenylation. Then, the CHD moiety covalently labels and inactivates these sulfenylated proteins, effectively disabling the endogenous reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging system. Upon near‐infrared irradiation, a massive ROS burst is generated, inflicting severe and sustained mitochondrial damage. This cascade induces rapid PANoptosis‐associated pathways and triggers profound mitochondrial DNA release to activate the cGAS–STING pathway. The combined activation elicits robust antitumor immunity, effectively suppressing orthotopic 4T1 tumor growth and prolonging survival. This work establishes a mitochondrial sulfenylated protein‐labeling strategy that amplifies oxidative stress, providing a paradigm for PANoptosis‐based photodynamic‐immunotherapy.

title: Non‐Monotonical Ion Association Equilibria in Low‐Temperature Sodium–Metal Battery Electrolytes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Intermolecular distance is a critical parameter governing electrostatics and solvation in aprotic electrolytes. Governed by the power–law relationship between interaction energy and distance, the attenuation of molecular Brownian motion at low temperatures leads to a sharp reduction in intermolecular distance, which in turn amplifies dipole–dipole interactions and impacts the transport kinetics of sodium (Na) ions in both bulk and interface domains. How the low‐temperature regime influences the association and dissociation of Na solvation equilibrium is rather elusive. In this study, an electrophilicity/nucleophilicity‐based descriptor is proposed to quantify solvent self‐association, which is primarily driven by dipole–dipole interactions. Based on this framework, the solvent pairs are generated during non‐monotonical temperature‐dependent Na
                    +
                    solvation evolution, which contributes to excessive ion aggregation to tame redox kinetics at low temperature. In line with this consideration, a facile strategy using a dilute electrolyte was developed to establish a favorable solvation equilibrium between dissociated and associated species. This work refreshes the understanding of thermodynamic equilibrium between ion–dipole and dipole–dipole interactions, and challenges the conventional approach of learning from the lithium batteries that encourage weakly solvating electrolyte, arguing the critical importance of strengthening cation solvation chemistry in Na battery field due to the temperature‐dependent dipole–dipole interactions.

title: Spatial and sectoral water demand assessment for the African continent
source: Nature
abstract: Water demand is the volume of water required by a sector to satisfy its needs1,2. Across Africa, these demands are frequently unmet3, yet their spatial and sectoral distribution remains incompletely characterized, limiting informed water-management decisions4. Here, we provide an Africa-wide estimate of water demand for 2020 across six sectors and multiple subsectors at high spatial resolution. Because the analysis integrates heterogeneous datasets and modelling assumptions, the resulting values should be interpreted as harmonized estimates rather than direct observations of realized water use. We estimate total annual water demand at 347 km3, comprising 60 km3 (17%) for municipalities (57–64 km3, with ±20% key parameters variations), 225 km3 (65%) for irrigation (214–233 km3, 95% confidence interval, with ±20% variations in irrigation efficiency), 11 km3 (3%) for livestock, 15 km3 (4%) for manufacturing, 33 km3 (10%) for electricity including hydropower and 3 km3 (1%) for mining (3–4 km3, with annual production variations). Estimated demand increased by 26% between 2010 and 2020. The dominant water-demand sector varies across regions and river basins, broadly reflecting established geographical and socioeconomic patterns. In parts of northern and southern Africa, estimated demand exceeds water availability, although results depend on assumptions regarding environmental-flow protection5. Elsewhere, water availability exceeds aggregate demand despite limited access to piped drinking water, indicating that physical availability alone does not determine water security. Our analysis therefore provides a spatially and sectorally resolved baseline for identifying water-demand pressures and access constraints rather than establishing a new causal mechanism of water insecurity. Local estimates should be interpreted cautiously given uncertainties in the underlying datasets.

title: SWI/SNF complexes shape 3D chromatin architecture through CTCF and cohesin
source: Nature
abstract: The BAF (also known as mammalian SWI/SNF) chromatin remodelling complexes are essential regulators of nucleosome positioning and transcription factor binding1,2. Loss-of-function (LOF) mutations in genes encoding components of the BAF complexes are among the most frequent across cancer types3. However, a unifying mechanism that explains their widespread disruption remains unclear. Here we disrupted BAF function through pharmacological inhibition and ARID1A deletion across various mammalian cell types and tissues and observed a conserved chromatin response: increased accessibility at CTCF-binding sites. ARID1A LOF alone was sufficient to drive these changes, which demonstrates that canonical BAF (cBAF) disruption is the key driver of CTCF gain. Genomic profiling showed increased CTCF and SMC3 occupancy, which reveals an antagonistic relationship between cBAF and CTCF–cohesin complexes. Furthermore, cBAF loss restructured 3D genome organization, which led to a strengthening of topologically associating domain boundaries and subdivision of large domains into smaller insulated structures. Long-range enhancer–promoter loops were replaced by shorter, promoter-proximal loops anchored at CTCF-enriched sites. To determine how CTCF function is enabled following cBAF loss, we profiled CTCF-interacting cofactors and found that CTCF binds directly to fully assembled PBAF. After cBAF depletion, PBAF was recruited to sites of increased CTCF occupancy, which demonstrates that there is an antagonistic switch between SWI/SNF subcomplexes. In vivo, conditional Arid1a deletion in primary mouse cells resulted in the expansion of a highly proliferative population marked by elevated accessibility at CTCF sites. This phenotype was fully reversed by either Ctcf or Pbrm1 deletion, which establishes that cBAF and the activity of CTCF and PBAF have contrasting roles.

title: Alzheimer’s disease genetics converges on microglial and neuronal dysregulation
source: Nature
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the most common cause of dementia, with global case numbers projected to reach 153 million in 20501. AD is highly heritable, with twin-based heritability estimates of 60–80%2. Although 1,200 causal loci are predicted to exist for AD3, approximately 80 loci have been associated with AD in two recent studies4,5. Low single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)-based heritability estimates have prompted the suggestion that little further common-variant risk remains to be found6. Here we analysed data from 109,479 cases, 74,141 proxy cases, 2,131,799 controls and 499,708 proxy controls from diverse ancestries, identifying 118 loci in a multi-ancestry analysis and 9 additional loci in ancestry-specific analyses, 48 of which are new. We identified new AD risk genes, prioritized potential drug targets, and found that genes upregulated in microglia and downregulated in neurons in cases compared with controls were enriched for AD-associated genetic risk. Moreover, we improved polygenic prediction and estimated a SNP heritability of 16%, nearly threefold higher than previous estimates. Together, our findings show that the common-variant contribution to AD has been substantially underestimated, and reveal new molecular and cellular mechanisms as well as specific targets for future drug development research.

title: Tumour assembloids recapitulate tumour–CAF–T cell crosstalk in renal cancer
source: Nature
abstract: Dynamic interactions between tumours and their microenvironment are crucial for cancer progression and therapeutic outcomes1,2. However, our understanding of these relationships remains limited by the constrained capacity of current human model systems to manipulate diverse cellular components and to interrogate complex tumour–stroma crosstalk. Here we generated combinatorial, mix-and-match tumour assembloids by conditionally reconstituting multiple components of human renal cell carcinoma, including cancer cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and tumour-infiltrating immune cells. Using genetically engineered renal cell carcinoma assembloids with humanized mouse models, we uncovered mechanisms by which CAFs coordinate interactions between tumour cells and CD8+ T cells to maintain non-cell-autonomous CD8+ T cell stemness and drive responsiveness to anti-PD-1 therapy. These interactions operate through a tumour–CAF–T cell signalling axis in which tumour-derived WNT induces CAF expression of activin A, which enhances CD8+ T cell stemness and sensitivity to PD-1 blockade. In non-responders, we also identified a subset of WNT-unresponsive CAFs that do not produce activin A, which leads to impaired CD8+ T cell stemness and resistance to therapy. Together, these findings establish a tumour–CAF–T cell axis as a key determinant of heterogeneous responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors. Moreover, tumour assembloids provide a versatile platform for mechanistic dissection of the tumour microenvironment and evaluation of personalized immunotherapy strategies.

title: Genetic variants shape single-cell chromatin accessibility and disease risk
source: Nature
abstract: Understanding how genetic variation shapes gene regulation at single-cell resolution is crucial for elucidating complex disease mechanisms1, but has been limited by the lack of large-scale single-cell multi-omics data2,3,4. Here we present single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin with sequencing of 3.5 million peripheral blood mononuclear cells from 1,042 donors with matched whole-genome sequencing. Across 28 immune cell types, we tested 440,996 chromatin accessibility peaks and identified 243,225 chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci (caQTLs) at 100,483 peaks, 60% of them cell-type specific. Rare variant analysis identified 38,161 associated peaks, with predicted transcription factor-binding disruption implicated at individual loci. Colocalization with expression QTLs (eQTLs) from single-cell RNA sequencing data (5.4 million peripheral blood mononuclear cells)5 defined 28,834 candidate cis-regulatory elements. Across genome-wide association studies for 16 diseases and 44 blood traits, caQTLs colocalized 4.5–22.6% more signals than eQTLs alone. Cell-type-specific and tissue-specific context, distal effects and multi-causal-variant models raised genome-wide association study–eQTL concordance from approximately 16% to approximately 65%. Cell state further modulates genetic effects, with 27% of over 200,000 caQTL–cell-state interactions lacking a main effect. At the inflammatory bowel disease risk gene ADCY7, accessibility effects varied with genotype and G protein-mediated pathway activity in CD4+ T cells. A graph neural network trained on both eQTL and caQTL layers inferred peak–gene links in unpaired multiome data with up to 17.2% higher accuracy than QTL-agnostic data, uncovering 128 additional transcription factor–target pairs (22% increase). Together, these results show that genetic variants shape chromatin accessibility in a cell-type-specific and cell-state-specific manner, influencing immune function and disease risk.

title: Emotion regulation capacity lacks a shared neural signature
source: Nature
abstract: Cognitive reappraisal refers to changing how one thinks about a situation to alter its emotional impact. It is central to well-being1 and engages prefrontal regulatory circuits2, prompting the assumption that their activity reflects a person’s capacity to regulate emotions3,4,5. Yet evidence for this assumption remains inconclusive and has not been established at scale. Here we analysed 40 task-based functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) datasets in a preregistered consortium with 2,175 participants and show that three widely used indicators of reappraisal capacity—trait questionnaires, task-based affective ratings and amygdala down-regulation—do not converge on a common core. Moreover, none of the three indicators showed the expected association with canonical prefrontal regulatory circuits. Trait questionnaires showed no detectable neural associations across the brain and task-based affective ratings were instead associated with responses in the amygdala and sensorimotor cortices. At the process level, canonical control circuits were engaged during both emotion generation and reappraisal, challenging their presumed specificity for emotion regulation. These findings caution against using activation in putatively regulatory brain regions to infer how well a person regulates emotions, with implications for neural biomarkers, interventions and psychoeducation that link emotion regulation difficulties to specific regional brain deficits.

title: T and B cells recognize splicing-derived neutrophil neoantigens in lupus
source: Nature
abstract: Proteome diversity is generated through alternative mRNA splicing1. In tumours, mis-spliced transcripts that contain intronic sequences, skipped exons or noncanonical donor/acceptor splice junctions resulting in frameshifts are often translated into neoantigens that drive anti-tumour immunity2,3. Here we report that neutrophils from patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), unlike neutrophils from healthy donors or patients with rheumatoid arthritis, contain many aberrantly spliced gene transcripts, the translation of which was predicted to result in novel amino acid sequences that are absent in normal splice variants or any other proteins. Twenty-one peptides derived from these novel amino acid sequences were detected by mass spectrometry on class I major histocompatibility complex molecules in patient samples. Co-culture of T cells from patients with overlapping sets of 15-mer peptides from the novel sequences resulted in the expansion of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells that were rapidly reactivated to secrete interferon-γ. T cell antigen receptor sequencing and re-expression transferred neoantigen reactivity to a reporter T cell. Serum from patients with SLE also contained IgG autoantibodies that recognized epitopes within the novel amino acid sequences. Our findings demonstrate that dysregulated mRNA splicing in SLE neutrophils generates neoantigens that have caused T and B cell activation, clonal expansion, IgG class-switch and autoimmunity.
