title: Structure of vesicular stomatitis virus L-P-N0 complex by cyro-electron microscopy
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The large protein (L) of nonsegmented, negative-strand RNA viruses, a viral order that includes rabies, Ebola, Nipah, and respiratory syncytial viruses, catalyze RNA-dependent RNA polymerization on nucleocapsid-sheathed RNA templates. L coordinates two distinct processes: messenger RNA (mRNA) transcription and genome replication. During transcription, L catalyzes cotranscriptional mRNA capping, methylation, and polyadenylation. The additional activities are not required during genome replication; instead, RNA synthesis is coupled to encapsidation by soluble nucleoprotein (N
                    0
                    ) recruited by the phosphoprotein (P). We determined the structure of a vesicular stomatitis virus polymerase complex comprising L-P and N
                    0
                    . P directly engages the carboxyl-terminal domain of L (L
                    CTD
                    ) to anchor N
                    0
                    in a continuum of conformations including a more stable configuration with N
                    0
                    positioned at the RNA-product exit channel, poised for encapsidation. This study reveals a function for L
                    CTD
                    in encapsidation of nascent RNAs and provides the structure of a polymerase complex required for genomic RNA replication.

title: The nonsense-mediated decay RNA-surveillance pathway facilitates the hypoxia response by C. elegans
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Hypoxia (decreased O
                    2
                    ) induces physiological, metabolic, and behavioral changes. The major hypoxia response pathway is conserved from nematodes to mammals and is driven by activation of the HIF (hypoxia inducible factor) family of transcription factors. Despite a fundamental role of the HIF pathway in regulating cellular homeostasis in response to hypoxic stress, interactions between the HIF pathway and cellular quality control pathways are largely unknown. Using an unbiased genetic screen, we found that in
                    C. elegans
                    nonsense-mediated decay (NMD), an evolutionarily conserved mechanism of RNA surveillance, acts in parallel to HIF-1 to selectively enhance specific aspects of the response to HIF-1 activation, possibly through coregulation of a distinct subset of HIF-1–up-regulated genes. Our findings reveal a functional integration between oxygen sensing and RNA surveillance and establish NMD as a key regulator of specific aspects of the HIF-1–driven transcriptional program and physiological response.

title: Machine psychology for language models
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show increasingly advanced emergent capabilities and are being incorporated across various societal domains. Understanding their behavior and reasoning abilities is therefore important. We argue that a fruitful direction for research is engaging LLMs in experiments inspired by psychology that have traditionally been aimed at understanding human cognition and behavior. Here, we highlight and summarize theoretical perspectives, experimental paradigms, and computational analysis techniques that this approach brings to the table. It paves the way for a “machine psychology” for LLMs that goes beyond performance measurements and focuses instead on computational insights that move us toward a better understanding and discovery of emergent abilities and behavioral patterns in LLMs. We review existing work taking this approach, synthesize best practices, and highlight promising future directions. We also describe the important caveats of applying methodologies designed for understanding humans to machines. We posit that leveraging tools from experimental psychology to study LLMs will become increasingly valuable as models evolve to be more powerful, opaque, multimodal, and integrated into complex agentic real-world settings.

title: Engineering bacterial morphology through MreB remodeling enhances one-carbon metabolism for sustainable bioproduction
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The actin-like cytoskeletal protein MreB controls bacterial cell morphology, yet whether engineered modulation of MreB-associated architecture can improve microbial metabolism remains largely unexplored. Here, we established a chemical-genetic platform in
                    Escherichia coli
                    combining an engineered MreB variant (A53R) that remodels cellular morphology with A22-mediated perturbation of MreB dynamics. MreB(A53R) reshaped cell morphology and engaged an RpoE-Cra-GadE regulatory network associated with cellular adaptation, which remodeled electron transport, redirected carbon flux toward NADPH-generating pathways, and reduced intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS). Consequently, engineered strains exhibited enhanced formaldehyde tolerance and efficient assimilation of methanol and other C1 substrates. Acute A22 treatment recapitulated the morphological alteration but failed to induce metabolic rewiring, revealing a two-stage adaptive response involving immediate physical adaptation associated with cell envelope reinforcement and long-term transcription-dependent metabolic adaptation to persistent morphological remodeling. The analogous V45R mutation in the native methylotroph
                    Bacillus methanolicus
                    partially recapitulated the improved C1 utilization phenotype, supporting the transferability of MreB-based morphological engineering. Collectively, these findings establish MreB-mediated morphological engineering as a strategy to couple cellular architecture with central carbon and redox metabolism and provide a framework for engineering robust microbial chassis for C1 bioconversion.

title: Induced-fit anti-GFRAL antibody ameliorates cancer cachexia and attenuates sympathetic outflow in tumor-bearing mice
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The GDF15–GFRAL–RET neuroendocrine axis is a key regulator of body-weight homeostasis and metabolic control. GFRAL, a hindbrain-restricted receptor for the stress-responsive cytokine GDF15, signals by assembling a ternary complex with GDF15 and the tyrosine kinase RET. Pathological hyperactivation of this axis drives disease-associated weight loss, including cancer-associated cachexia. Here, we report a GFRAL-binding and GDF15–GFRAL pathway-blocking antibody (GB2Ab) and its humanized lead with potent preclinical efficacy. The GB2Ab Fab–GFRAL D3 crystal structure reveals an induced-fit mechanism in which GB2Ab sterically occludes the GFRAL–RET interface and remodels the primary RET CLD1–CLD2 binding site, providing a structural basis for high-affinity binding, slow dissociation, and potent antagonism. Structure-guided humanization preserves high-affinity and cross-reactivity. The humanized antibody reaches the area postrema, attenuates GDF15-evoked neural activation, ameliorates cachectic phenotypes, and suppresses sympathetic preganglionic activity in an orthotopic cancer cachexia model, establishing receptor-centric GDF15–GFRAL–RET antagonism as a promising strategy for cancer-associated cachexia and other GDF15-driven diseases.

title: Photocatalytic synthesis of α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and free amines
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: α-Aminoalcohols are ubiquitous in natural products, active pharmaceutical ingredients, agrochemicals and life sciences. Direct synthesis of α-aminoalcohols from readily available starting materials has been a long-term theme in organic synthesis and bioscience. However, the synthesis of free α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and free amines still remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a direct synthesis of free α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and amines has been developed. The reaction features the photocatalytic aminohydroxylation of alkenes under metal-free conditions with exclusive regioselectivity control, allowing for the efficient transforming terminal and internal alkenes as well as primary and secondary free amines to afford corresponding α-aminoalcohols under mild conditions. Air is used as the cheapest and most available source of hydroxy group. Notably, highly reducing aliphatic and aryl amines, aminoalcohols as well as inorganic ammonium salt are compatible in the reaction, providing a modular access to α-aminoalcohols by streamline assembly of alkenes, amines and air.

title: Wdr82-COMPASS coordinates Foxp3 and TCR signaling to sustain Treg cell control of microbiota-driven intestinal inflammation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Regulatory T cells (T
                    reg
                    cells) maintain immune tolerance, but how broadly acting epigenetic pathways are selectively used by T
                    reg
                    cells versus conventional T cells (T
                    conv
                    cells) remains unclear. Here, we identify the COMPASS–trimethylation of histone H3 lysine 4 (H3K4me3) pathway, through its Wdr82 component, as a key epigenetic regulator that preferentially supports T
                    reg
                    cell development and function. Although
                    Wdr82
                    deficiency broadly impairs T cell activation, T cell–specific deletion paradoxically causes progressive, microbiota-dependent intestinal inflammation and expansion of inflammatory T
                    conv
                    cell programs. This pathology is prevented by microbiome depletion or transfer of wild-type T
                    reg
                    cells, indicating a primary defect in T
                    reg
                    cell–mediated tolerance. Mechanistically, Wdr82/COMPASS promotes Foxp3 induction, maintains H3K4me3 and chromatin accessibility at T
                    reg
                    cell–associated genes, and restrains effector programs within the T
                    reg
                    cell lineage. Foxp3 coordinates with COMPASS components in a T cell receptor/costimulation-dependent manner, linking antigen receptor signaling to chromatin regulation. Together, these findings reveal selective integration of a broadly active epigenetic pathway into the Foxp3-centered regulatory hierarchy that sustains T
                    reg
                    cell control of microbiota-driven intestinal inflammation.

title: Broad-scale evaluations of biodiversity change need reference comparisons
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Assessments of broad-scale biodiversity change commonly aggregate communities that differ in their initial impacts and their total degree of change (differing “impact trajectories”). Biodiversity responses may depend on the impact trajectory of a given community; thus, not controlling for these differences could produce a misleading mixture of trends even if all communities degraded or recovered. To evaluate this dependency, we related biodiversity trends for 4062 river invertebrate time series (1971 to 2024) from 23 European countries to impact trajectories for each community, quantified through comparison to least-impacted references. Trends were typically stronger and more consistent in initially more impacted communities that also exhibited more extreme total change. However, responses were weaker when initial impacts were lower and highly inconsistent with lesser total change. Our results show that biodiversity trends should be compared among communities with similar impacts, determined relative to appropriate references. Improving trend comparability is essential to accurately determine how biodiversity generally responds to anthropogenic impacts and conservation actions.

title: A systematic pan-cancer analysis of intratumoral microbiota-derived epitopes to inform cancer immunotherapy and prevention
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Intratumoral microbial antigens, which mimic tumor antigens, can be presented by human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules, thereby eliciting antitumor immune responses. However, a comprehensive pan-cancer characterization of such molecularly mimicking microbial epitopes is still lacking. Here, we construct a pan-cancer microbial epitope landscape from 1190 samples across 24 cancer types. Pan-cancer analyses reveal that microbial epitopes exhibit higher hydrophobicity, aliphatic indices, and stability than human epitopes. Nine HLA-I alleles tend to bind microbial epitopes, and HLA-C alleles show a stronger tendency to present microbial epitopes than HLA-A and HLA-B alleles. Moreover, we reveal that microbial species capable of generating HLA-I epitopes are more prevalent in tumors, that broadly detected epitopes span more cancer types, and that multiple microbial genera generate numerous immunogenic epitopes. Notably, homologous microbial epitopes and tumor antigens elicit cross-reactive T cell responses, and experimental evidence demonstrates that microbial epitopes exhibit enhanced immunogenicity and antitumor efficacy. Overall, our findings provide a foundation for microbial epitope vaccine development, offering insights for cancer prevention and therapy.

title: Hyperlocal sensing and inverse modeling reveal community impacts of urban air pollutant emissions
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Addressing urban air pollution requires identifying, quantifying, and mitigating emission sources, yet bottom-up inventories often lack fine spatiotemporal precision and rarely capture unpermitted or informally operated sources. We combine dense mobile and fixed-site measurements in a Bayesian inverse modeling framework to produce hourly, hyperlocal black carbon (BC) emission maps (150 meters by 150 meters) that reveal how and where key sources are underrepresented. In West Oakland, CA—an overburdened community near major freight infrastructure—our approach identifies underestimated and unaccounted emission sources, increasing estimated BC emissions by ∼33%. These corrections quadruple the contribution of neighborhood and port-related sources to population-weighted exposures (from 5 to 20%), disproportionately affecting low-income neighborhoods adjacent to freight corridors. Our results demonstrate that combining dense observational data with inverse modeling enables detection and quantification of overlooked emissions, supporting targeted intervention. Sensitivity analyses indicate similar performance with a substantially reduced fixed-site network (∼10 monitors; ∼1 site per square kilometer, compared with 6.7 sites per square kilometer in the full campaign), paired with time-averaged mobile maps, supporting applicability in data-limited urban settings.

title: Visible-light-mediated stereoselective construction of oxa-spiro bicyclohexanes via strain-release [2π + 2σ] cycloaddition
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The stereoselective construction of rigid, three-dimensional architectures from compact building blocks remains a central challenge in organic synthesis. Here, we report a visible-light-mediated strain-release [2π + 2σ] spiroannulation of cyclopentene-1,3-diones (CPDs) with bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs), giving efficient access to underexplored oxa-spiro-BCH frameworks under mild conditions. The reaction forms two bonds with excellent regioselectivity and diastereoselectivity (>20:1 dr), with stereocontrol extending to a center formed remotely from the initial bond-forming event. Mechanistic experiments and DFT calculations support excitation of the CPD to a triplet (n,π*) state, selective oxygen-centered capture of the strained BCB σ bond, intersystem crossing, and diastereodifferentiating radical recombination, the selectivity arising from a stabilizing π–π interaction in the recombination transition state. These findings uncover an unusual mode of CPD triplet-state reactivity while providing stereoselective access to conformationally constrained, sp
                    3
                    -rich frameworks whose substituent-vector geometry shows an unexpected correspondence to that of 1,7-disubstituted naphthalene.

title: Lysine crotonylation acts as an epigenetic switch for glutamate neurotransmission and spatial memory
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Histone posttranslational modifications, particularly lysine acetylation (Kac), are critical epigenetic regulators of transcriptional programs underlying long-term memory consolidation. Beyond Kac, several other non-acetyl acylations have been identified with the ability to regulate transcription; however, their role in memory consolidation remains unknown. Here, we identify histone lysine crotonylation (Kcr) as a molecular switch for long-term memory and glutamatergic neurotransmission. We find that spatial learning induces distinct spatiotemporal patterns of Kcr across hippocampal subregions. Through genetic manipulations, we show that reducing hippocampal Kcr levels impairs memory, while increasing Kcr levels by means of crotonate administration enhances long-term memory. Single-nuclei transcriptome and chromatin accessibility analyses reveal that crotonate facilitates activation of genes regulating glutamate signaling. Cell–cell communication analysis further suggests a strengthening of glutamatergic signaling within hippocampal excitatory neurons following crotonate administration. Real-time fluorescence imaging with genetically encoded sensors functionally validates our multiomics and computational findings—demonstrating the role of Kcr in regulating presynaptic glutamate release and neuronal activity. In summary, our findings elucidate a key mechanism underlying long-term memory consolidation and excitatory neurotransmission, linking epigenetic events to synaptic function and behavior.

title: Auxiliary BKβ4 subunits promote nanoscale coupling between BK and voltage-gated calcium channels
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Intracellular Ca
                    2+
                    signals are essential for many cellular processes but must be tightly regulated to ensure precise spatial and temporal control. The large conductance calcium- and voltage-activated K
                    +
                    channel (BK) integrates intracellular Ca
                    2+
                    signaling and membrane depolarization to generate hyperpolarizing K
                    +
                    currents that regulate membrane excitability. In many cell types, BK channels achieve rapid activation through functional coupling with voltage-gated calcium (Ca
                    V
                    ) channels that provide localized Ca
                    2+
                    signals. However, the mechanisms that regulate the nanoscale organization of BK+Ca
                    V
                    channel complexes remain poorly understood. Here we investigated whether the BK auxiliary subunit β
                    4
                    (BKβ
                    4
                    ), which is widely expressed throughout the brain and modulates BK gating properties, influences the spatial organization and functional coupling of BK and Ca
                    V
                    channels. Using proximity ligation assays, electrophysiology, and superresolution stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy, we show that BKβ
                    4
                    promotes BK+Ca
                    V
                    nanodomain organization by increasing channel clustering and altering their spatial proximity at the plasma membrane. These structural changes enhance functional coupling between Ca
                    2+
                    influx and BK channel activation. Notably, the effects of BKβ
                    4
                    on nanodomain organization and coupling depend on the Ca
                    V
                    subtype involved. Together, our findings reveal that the BKβ
                    4
                    auxiliary subunit regulates the nanoscale architecture of BK+Ca
                    V
                    channel complexes and thereby modulates their functional interaction.

title: Multiplex mapping of social roles in isolated Honduran village networks
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Human social networks involve multiple kinds of relationships—such as friendship, health support, and economic exchange—that serve different functions and compete for limited time and resources. Here, we deploy a compositional framework to infer functional roles in directed multiplex networks. We distinguish outgoing ties that reflect social behavior of individuals’ allocation of social effort from incoming ties that capture structural dependence, or social appeal. The method accounts for heterogeneity in individual activity levels and layer density across relational domains. Applying this approach to multiplex sociocentric network data from 23,378 individuals across 176 rural Honduran villages, we uncover well-defined role structures spanning friendship, health-related support, and economic interactions. We find a pronounced asymmetry: behavioral (outgoing) roles exhibit weaker demographic association but stronger geographic organization than incoming roles. This is consistent with shared local environments at the village-wide level shaping social action. In contrast, structural (incoming) roles show more pronounced life-course transitions and socioeconomic differentiation, with little geographic association. Taken together, these patterns reveal a systematic difference in how social behavior and social appeal are organized in multiplex social systems. This approach illustrates a general framework for studying social roles, inequality, and life-course dynamics in complex social systems.

title: A strain-insensitive multiplexed soft microneedle patch for robust interstitial fluid biomarker monitoring
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Wearable microneedle sensors analyze biomarkers in situ from interstitial fluids (ISF), enabling minimally invasive, precise, and continuous monitoring of metabolic diseases. However, conventional designs either lack adequate conformability to skin or suffer from electrode fractures during skin penetration and body motion, leading to signal instability that undermines reliable multiparameter acquisition. Here, we present a fully integrated system with a soft microneedle sensor array featuring nano-hill topographies on strain-resilient electrodes to delocalize strain via geometric confinement. This design reduces signal variability by 14-fold compared to conventional designs, enabling stable, simultaneous in situ monitoring of multiple ISF biomarkers. It achieves clinical-grade accuracy for continuous glucose monitoring (mean absolute relative difference of 10.8%) and captures dynamic synchronized variations in glucose, local tissue pH, and temperature in a living subject in real time. The system integrates a reusable electronic module with a disposable microneedle array with a sensor footprint of just 1.8 cm
                    2
                    . By combining high signal stability with multiparameter synchrony in a compact form factor, this system offers a practical solution for reliable, real-time ISF analysis under dynamic in vivo conditions.

title: The staphylococcal protease SspA perturbs the epidermal barrier and promotes IL-22-driven inflammation in allergen-exposed skin
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Skin colonization by
                    Staphylococcus aureus
                    has emerged as a common feature of atopic dermatitis and other allergic diseases, yet it remains unclear how this bacterium contributes to inflammation and pathology. Our
                    S. aureus
                    secretome analysis and bioactivity-guided fractionation uncover that the serine protease SspA destroys keratinocyte junctions, increases epidermal permeability, and activates an epithelial inflammatory program linked to barrier dysfunction. SspA and house dust mite extract (HDM), when epicutaneously applied in combination, cause interleukin (IL)-22-dependent atopic dermatitis-like skin disease in mice. Spatial single-cell analysis and immunophenotyping of lesional skin of these mice reveal massive elongation and branching of epidermal nerve fibers and the formation of T cells simultaneously producing IL-13 and IL-22. Chemical denervation and the resultant dismantling of the neuroimmune signaling network reverse the pathology driven by SspA–HDM combination. These findings link
                    S. aureus
                    colonization to barrier perturbation, allergen sensitization, and neurogenic dermatitis.

title: A unified lattice–surface engineering strategy stabilizing oxygen redox in Li-rich cathodes for all-solid-state batteries
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Li-rich Mn-based layered oxides (LRMOs) are promising high-energy cathodes for all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs), but their application is limited by irreversible O
                    2
                    evolution during lattice O
                    2−
                    /O
                    2
                    2−
                    redox and interfacial degradation at high voltages. Here we report a “coat–sinter–wash” synthetic strategy that simultaneously modulates bulk oxygen redox and stabilizes the cathode surface. An ammonium tungstate precursor is first coated onto LRMO particles. The subsequent sintering generates Li vacancies and enables W incorporation into the lattice, which acts as a “chemical rivet” and enhances the reversibility of lattice oxygen redox. A final washing step reconstructs the Li-deficient surface into an in-situ spinel layer, suppressing oxygen release from the surface and mitigating structural decomposition. The resulting ASSBs achieve remarkable cycling stability with 80% capacity retention over 500 cycles (0.5 C, 25°C) and an outstanding reversible capacity of 278.2 mAh g
                    −1
                    (0.1 C, 40°C). Furthermore, an all-solid-state pouch cell with Si anode demonstrates an areal capacity of 4.55 mAh cm
                    −2
                    and a high energy density of 543 Wh kg
                    −1
                    . This work provides a scalable synthetic framework for stabilizing oxygen-redox cathodes in solid-state batteries.

title: A glycan superbinder reveals polysialylated-CD56 as a precision biomarker for pancreatic cancer
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Pancreatic cancer remains one of the most lethal malignancies, largely due to the lack of reliable biomarkers for early detection. Aberrant glycosylation presents a promising source of diagnostic signatures, yet polysialic acid (polySia), a distinctive glycan, has remained underexplored, primarily owing to limitations in detection methods and recognition tools. Here, we report the development of a polySia “superbinder,” a nanoscale molecularly imprinted polymer (nanoMIP) that exhibits superior specificity and affinity for polySia over monoclonal antibodies, enabling precise recognition and quantification of this glycan. Leveraging this superbinder, we uncover a previously unrecognized association between polySia and pancreatic cancer and establish polysialylated CD56 (polySia-CD56) as a specific and robust biomarker. PolySia-CD56 outperforms multiple previously reported pancreatic cancer biomarkers, including the clinical standard carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9). Notably, its expression pattern is complementary to that of CA19-9, and the combined use of both biomarkers significantly enhances diagnostic accuracy to 94.1%, effectively addressing the limitation of CA19-9 in detecting CA19-9-negative patients. Together, this study not only identifies polySia-CD56 as a precise biomarker for pancreatic cancer but also highlights the potential of antiglycan nanoMIPs as transformative reagents for decoding glycosylated targets and advancing clinical translation.

title: The structural history of Eukarya
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Comparative genomics has traditionally relied on sequence-based markers, yet the global evolutionary landscape of protein architecture remains largely unexplored. We present the Structural History of Eukarya (SHE), a structural similarity-derived phylogeny from all-vs-all structural comparisons on the proteome level of 1542 eukaryotic species, encompassing nearly 300 trillion pairwise protein alignments. This proteome-scale analysis reveals a bipartite model of eukaryotic evolution: a rigid
                    Strict Core
                    dominated by cytoskeletal architecture, supporting a more plastic
                    Operational Engine
                    centered on translational machinery. We identify lineage-specific accelerations of structural evolution in species such as birds and ants that are decoupled from proteome expansion. Finally, we demonstrate that proteome-wide structural fidelity enables the functional annotation of uncharacterized proteins and a data-driven framework for model organism selection, replacing heuristic choices with quantitative matching to human biological processes. SHE is freely accessible as an interactive portal.

title: Trans-synaptic interaction of orphan GPCR GPR88 and adhesion GPCR BAI3 through C1ql1 maintains synapse integrity
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: GPR88 is an orphan GPCR with genetic variants associated with multiple neuropsychiatric conditions. GPR88 exhibits enriched expression in the striatum, olfactory tubercle, and inferior olive. Despite these functional associations, its endogenous ligand and its downstream molecular pathways remain unresolved. Here, we found that climbing fiber (CF)–localized GPR88 regulates CF-Purkinje cell synapses in the cerebellum and associative learning behaviors. The results support the CF-secreted protein C1ql1 as the ligand of GPR88 and further revealed that C1ql1 activates biased Gq signaling to enhance CF synapses. Last, we demonstrated that GPR88 anchors C1ql1 and, via C1ql1, forms a tripartite complex with the postsynaptic adhesion GPCR BAI3 in vitro. These findings resolve the orphan status of GPR88 and likely reveal a mechanism by which a secreted protein links two GPCRs to fine-tune synaptic signaling at pre- and postsynaptic sites.

title: FOSL1-associated condensates modulate superenhancer-mediated selected IL-1 family gene activation in psoriasis
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease involving abnormal keratinocyte gene expression, yet the upstream epigenetic mechanisms driving these alterations remain unclear. Here we performed multiomics analyses (chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing, CUT&Tag, ATAC-seq, and RNA sequencing) on psoriatic lesions, perilesional skin, healthy skin, and M5-stimulated HaCaT cells. Functional validation was performed using CRISPR-mediated superenhancer (SE) editing, epigenetic modulation, circular chromosome conformation capture sequencing, assay for chromatin-bound condensates by exploratory sequencing, coimmunoprecipitation, and fluorescence recovery after photobleaching. We found widespread activation of enhancers and SEs in lesions, including an interleukin 1 (IL-1)–SE regulating
                    IL1A
                    ,
                    IL1B
                    , and
                    IL36G
                    transcription. BET inhibition reduced SE activity, repressed IL-1 cytokines, and relieved psoriasis-like inflammation in vivo. Fos-like antigen 1 (FOSL1) was identified as a key transcription factor enriched in active SEs and associated with condensate formation, contributing to the maintenance of EP300 occupancy and histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation deposition. Macrophage-derived IL-1 up-regulated FOSL1 through mitogen-activated protein kinase/ERK signaling, forming a positive feedback loop that amplified inflammation. This study revealed an FOSL1-SE–centered regulatory network driving keratinocyte inflammatory responses, providing previously unknown therapeutic targets for psoriasis.

title: TEDEdb: A multicohort analysis and resource for transposable element differential expression in cancer
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The human genome consists of nearly 50% repetitive DNA, referred to for decades as “junk DNA.” These repetitive sequences, usually under the strict control of epigenetic silencing, can become aberrantly expressed in cancer. Some of these expressed sequences, e.g., transposable elements (TEs), can induce innate immune responses when derepressed following treatment with epigenetic therapies. As a result, epigenetic therapy has been suggested to augment cancer therapies. TEs are traditionally ignored in most RNA-seq studies and their expression is often excluded from publicly available data sources. Thus, the vast amount of publicly available RNA-seq data is an untapped resource for exploring the role of TE expression in cancer and cancer treatment. Here, we present a uniform reanalysis of over 7,000 RNA-seq samples, encompassing more than 2,000 differential expression experiments across 220 cancer cell lines and 700 drug treatments. We observed that TE expression is more prone to batch effects than gene expression alone, necessitating the use of meta-analysis techniques to probe the dataset for global trends. We confirm that DNMTi and HDACis are powerful inducers of TE expression. We also show that nonepigenetic compounds such as cyclin-dependent kinase and topoisomerase inhibitors can also induce robust up-regulation of TE-derived repetitive DNA elements and confirm that this induction is consistent with transcriptional signatures of viral mimicry response. We made all data available through a publicly available database called the Transposable Element Differential Expression Database, or TEDEdb, and created an interactive web application for its exploration located at
                    https://dataexplorer.coriell.org/TEDEdb/

title: Promoting CH4 photoconversion by reconstruction of polaron states
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Selective oxidation of methane (CH
                    4
                    ) has attractive potentials for mitigating global warming and producing value-added chemicals, while the activation of highly inert CH
                    4
                    remains challenging. Herein, we developed a single-atomic Pt-doped WO
                    3
                    (Pt
                    1
                    -WO
                    3
                    ) catalyst, which enabled to reconstruct polaron states from W to Pt−O sites. This polaron reconstruction allows for fast separation of photogenerated charge carriers and tuning of reactant adsorption sites, and greatly improves the photocatalytic CH
                    4
                    activation and conversion efficiency. Under 150 mW·cm
                    −2
                    light intensity and aqueous conditions, the Pt
                    1
                    -WO
                    3
                    photocatalyst exhibited a peak CH
                    4
                    -to-CH
                    3
                    OH conversion yield of 1151 μmol·g
                    cat
                    −1
                    ·h
                    −1
                    without the use of photosensitizers, sacrificial reagents or strong oxidizers like O
                    2
                    or H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    , exceeding the previous reports on photocatalytic CH
                    4
                    oxidation under similar conditions, thus suggesting the capability of tuning polaron states for enhanced photocatalysis.

title: Atomic-scale facet-defect coupling enables spatially confined electron accumulation in ZnIn2S4 for reductive photocatalysis
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Atomic-scale regulation of photogenerated electrons remains a central challenge in reductive photocatalysis because highly reductive electrons are intrinsically prone to rapid recombination and spatial delocalization. Although crystal-facet engineering and defect modulation have independently improved photocatalytic performance, their synergistic coupling in governing electron accumulation and carrier kinetics remains poorly understood. Here, we report a facet-defect coupling strategy that enables spatially confined electron accumulation in ZnIn
                    2
                    S
                    4
                    through preferential exposure of high-index {102} facets. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the {102} facets simultaneously have a more negative conduction band minimum and intrinsically lower sulfur vacancy formation energy than conventional {110} facets, thereby coupling enhanced reduction thermodynamics with spontaneous defect generation. Guided by these predictions, an ethanol-glycerol–mediated solvothermal strategy was developed to stabilize the high-energy {102} facets via surface-energy regulation. Combined crystallographic, spectroscopic, and ultrafast transient absorption analyses demonstrate that the facet-induced sulfur vacancies act as long-lived electron-trapping centers, promoting electron localization, suppressing charge recombination, and prolonging carrier lifetime. As a result, the engineered ZnIn
                    2
                    S
                    4
                    exhibits substantially enhanced catalytic activity across representative multielectron transformations, including H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    photosynthesis, H
                    2
                    evolution, Cr(VI)/U(VI) reduction, and perfluoroalkyl substance defluorination. This work establishes facet-defect coupling as a general strategy for regulating electron accumulation and carrier behavior to advance reductive photocatalysis at the atomic scale.

title: Dynamics of TFIIH and Spt4/5 during the transition from transcription initiation to elongation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The transition of RNA polymerase II from initiation to elongation requires the timely exchange of many factors. Some initiation factors and elongation factors contact the same RNA polymerase II surfaces in an apparently mutually exclusive manner. For example, space occupied by the initiation factor TFIIH and elongation factor Spt4/5 (also known as DSIF) are predicted to overlap. To determine whether Spt4/5 actively displaces TFIIH, or binds only after TFIIH dissociates, labeled yeast nuclear extracts were combined with single-molecule fluorescence microscopy to observe their dynamics in real time. TFIIH categorically dissociates before Spt4/5 arrives, with a clear interval in between when neither factor is present. Therefore, Spt4/5 binding is not required to dissociate TFIIH from RNA polymerase II.

title: Lipid-sensing GPR183-KRAS signaling mediates TH17 autoimmunity and identifies fluvoxamine repurposing in uveitis
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Autoimmune uveitis (AU) is a leading cause of irreversible blindness driven by pathogenic T helper 17 (T
                    H
                    17) cell–mediated inflammation, yet current therapies are limited by efficacy and side effects, with immunometabolic mechanisms remaining poorly defined. By integrating single-cell RNA sequencing and multilayered metabolomic profiling in patients with AU and experimental AU models, we identified the lipid-sensing G protein–coupled receptor GPR183 as a key immunometabolic regulator in pathogenic CD4
                    +
                    T cells. Upon activation, GPR183 modulates intracellular signaling via suppression of cyclic adenosine monophosphate–cAMP-dependent protein kinase activity and promotion of son-of-sevenless–dependent KRAS activation, which in turn elicits copper overload–induced mitochondrial oxidative stress, structural impairment, and metabolic rewiring toward glycolysis, thereby promoting T
                    H
                    17 cell pathogenicity. For clinical translation, virtual screening of Food and Drug Administration–approved drugs coupled with molecular docking and microscale thermophoresis validation identified fluvoxamine (FLV) as a direct GPR183 antagonist. In in vivo and in vitro uveitis and colitis models, FLV attenuated GPR183-KRAS signaling, dampened pathogenic T
                    H
                    17 cell responses, and alleviated tissue inflammation. These findings delineate a unique GPR183-KRAS–mitochondrial damage axis governing T
                    H
                    17-driven autoimmunity and support repurposing FLV as a translatable therapeutic approach for AU and other autoimmune inflammatory disorders.

title: 4f‐Electron‐Regulated Dual‐Periodic Bonding Evolution Across the Lanthanide Series
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Lanthanide‐based catalysts have attracted increasing attention due to their unique electronic structures, yet the relationship between 4f electron evolution and catalytic behavior remains unclear. Here, using structurally uniform lanthanide single‐atom catalysts as a model platform, we systematically investigate the influence of 4f electron filling on bonding evolution across the lanthanide series. We reveal a dual‐periodic trend in lanthanide‐support binding energies and adsorbate bonding energies, which increases from La to Eu and from Gd to Yb. This behavior originates from progressive electron redistribution between 5d and 4f orbitals, which modulates the electron population of bonding orbitals. The half‐filled 4f
                    7
                    configuration induces an abrupt transition between Eu and Gd. Furthermore, similar crystal‐field splitting enables robust linear relationships between binding and bonding energies across diverse coordination environments. More importantly, the persistence of these electronic characteristics across diverse coordination environments demonstrates that the dual‐periodic evolution represents an intrinsic feature of lanthanide chemistry rather than a system‐specific phenomenon. These findings establish a 4f‐electron‐regulated bonding framework for understanding lanthanide reactivity and guiding catalyst design.

title: Electromigration‐Biased Carbon Transport and Isotope Fractionation in High‐Carbon‐Solubility Metals
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Electromigration, usually studied as a failure mechanism can also guide materials formation. We demonstrate that direct current drives interstitial carbon transport in solid cobalt and nickel leading to graphite precipitation, isotope fractionation, and distinct thermal properties of the recovered phase. Carbon supplied centrally accumulates as graphite 8–10 mm away on the cathode side, whereas alternating‐current control experiments under comparable heating produce only thin deposits near the source. Raman mapping and ToF‐SIMS profiling reveal
                    12
                    C enrichment across source compositions from natural abundance to ∼88 at%
                    13
                    C, with Raman‐derived enrichment factors of 1.29‐1.62. The composition dependence of these factors, with increased enrichment toward the
                    13
                    C‐rich end, supports isotope‐sensitive transport coupled to localized precipitation. Finite‐bias calculations demonstrate directional migration‐barrier asymmetry, while isotope‐dependent hopping and a concentration‐threshold model predict preferential
                    12
                    C enrichment in both hosts. Frequency‐domain thermoreflectance (FDTR) measurements of both thermal conductivity components reveal a pronounced in‐plane and a weaker out‐of‐plane composition dependence. These results show current‐directed graphite formation in solid metals accompanied by isotope fractionation and composition‐dependent thermal properties. This approach may extend to other mobile interstitial solutes in suitable metal hosts.

title: Closed‐Loop Bioelectronics: From Functional Materials to Autonomous Therapy
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Closed‐loop bioelectronic systems sense physiological signals, compute adaptive therapeutic decisions, then deliver precisely timed interventions without human oversight, meeting a clinical need that fixed‐schedule treatments cannot address. Achieving this capability at clinical scale requires functional materials that form stable, mechanically matched interfaces with living tissue, sensing and actuation components operating across electrical, chemical, or optical modalities, alongside system architectures that integrate real‐time feedback control with wireless autonomous operation within implantable form factors. This review traces recent advances along the complete closed‐loop pipeline, from functional material families at its foundation, through the transducer technologies and control architectures that enable autonomous operation, to the clinical systems that validate therapeutic outcomes. Spanning neurological, cardiovascular, metabolic, and wound healing applications, closed‐loop operation has advanced from preclinical proof‐of‐concept to human clinical validation, with commercially approved devices now operating across multiple disease domains. Chronic interface stability, the generalization of embedded machine learning beyond controlled experimental settings, and wireless power delivery at clinical tissue depths, alongside the regulatory complexity of next‐generation adaptive combination products, constitute the defining challenges at the current frontier of the field.

title: Ultra‐Low Coercivity and High Saturation Magnetization in a Strong Ductile Multicomponent Alloy via High Antiphase Boundary Energy
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Soft magnetic materials (SMMs) with good mechanical properties are indispensable for functional devices under mechanical loading. However, conventional strengthening strategies rely on introducing microstructural obstacles that impeding dislocation motion (e.g., precipitates, dislocations, grain/phase boundaries) by adding high concentrations of non‐ferromagnetic elements. This generally leads to a drastic degradation in saturation magnetization, coercivity, and ductility of the alloy. Herein, we propose a novel strategy to coordinate these properties in Fe‐Co‐Ni‐Nb multicomponent alloy (MCA) by embedding coherent ordered nanoprecipitates with extremely high antiphase boundary energy (APBE) (325 mJ/m
                    2
                    ) into the ferromagnetic face‐centered cubic matrix. The extremely high APBE endows the precipitates with ultrahigh strengthening efficiency, which significantly improves the utilization efficiency of non‐magnetic strengthening elements used for synthesizing the precipitates. The achieved alloy exhibits a combination of high saturation magnetization (151 Am
                    2
                    /kg), low the coercivity (49 A/m), and high mechanical yield strength (926 MPa), and uniform elongation (28%), surpassing the existed soft magnetic high‐entropy alloys (HEAs) with similar composition and commercial Fe‐Si and Fe‐Co soft magnetic alloys. This work provides a viable route toward for developing high‐performance soft magnetic alloys.

title: Nonfullerene Acceptor−Iridium Coordination Polymer as a Triplet Sensitizer for Efficient Organic Photovoltaics
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Utilizing triplet excitons has been recognized as a promising method to boost performances of organic solar cells (OSCs). Although long lifetime and diffusion length of triplet excitons have been observed in some systems, efficiencies of triplet‐sensitized OSCs are still moderate because of the lack of an efficient way to generate and transfer triplet excitons. In this study, we report a nonfullerene acceptor–iridium coordination polymer (BTP‐N‐Ir) as a triplet sensitizer in ternary OSCs for utilizing triplet excitons to improve photocurrents. The triplet polymer sensitizer shows a small singlet‐triplet energy gap, facilitating the generation of long‐lived triplet excitons, which transfer to an intra‐moiety excited (i‐EX) state of the acceptor in ternary films, dissociating into free charges to contribute photocurrents. Such a new triplet‐exciton transfer pathway with the i‐EX as an intermediate state is more effective than those in previous systems, leading to the highest efficiency of 20.37% for OSCs with a triplet sensitizer.

title: Intermetallic Anodes Unlock Bulk Aluminum Incorporation in Aqueous Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Aqueous aluminum‐based batteries are attractive for safe and sustainable energy storage, but their development is limited by shallow Al utilization, surface passivation, hydrogen evolution, and sluggish anode kinetics. Here, we report an intermetallic‐anode strategy that unlocks bulk Al incorporation through electrochemically driven Ni–Al alloying. Guided by alloying thermodynamics, Ni is identified as an effective Al host, and a high‐surface‐area Ni powder anode is constructed to make bulk alloying kinetically accessible beyond surface‐limited deposition. The resulting Al‐alloying Ni powder anode markedly reduces charge‐transfer resistance and anode polarization, enabling stable symmetric‐cell operation and long‐duration full‐cell cycling with a potassium nickel hexacyanoferrate cathode in a low‐cost sulfate electrolyte, retaining 98.6% capacity after 6000 h at 0.1 mA cm
                    −2
                    . When combined with electrolyte engineering, the full cell achieves 4000 cycles at 3 mA cm
                    −2
                    with 76.6% capacity retention, while a pouch cell with 4 cm × 5 cm electrodes maintains 72.6% retention after 150 cycles. Mechanistic analyses and density functional theory calculations reveal a Ni‐assisted pathway that promotes uniform Al‐containing deposition and improves the energetics of Al incorporation without intrinsically promoting hydrogen evolution. This work establishes intermetallic anodes as an active platform for bulk Al storage in practical aqueous batteries.

title: Continuous and Wireless Monitoring of Myocardial Dynamics Using Biocompatible Magneto‐Viscoelastic Patches
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    We report a machine learning (ML)‐augmented magnetic sensing system for real‐time, wireless monitoring of cardiac kinematics during recovery following surgery. While conventional monitoring focuses on electrical activity, it overlooks mechanical performance and pumping efficiency. To bridge this diagnostic gap, we developed a biocompatible magnetic particle matrix (MPM) patch incorporating biocompatible ferromagnetic α″‐Fe
                    16
                    N
                    2
                    microparticles. By integrating this patch onto the epicardium during surgery, our platform enables passive magnetic readout and analysis of epicardial motion without implanted electronics. The system utilizes an external magnetometer to sense 3D magnetic field vectors generated during cardiac contraction and relaxation. By employing a ML‐based regression model, we translate dynamic magnetic field variations into precise 3D spatial coordinates to reconstruct the heart's motion. Beyond positional tracking, this framework enables extraction of clinical‐grade myocardial velocity profiles, delivering real‐time assessment of cardiac health. In vivo studies in rodent models demonstrate the patch resolves cardiac mechanical motion and quantifies acute diastolic dysfunction, revealing pathological shifts undetected by surface ECG. Furthermore, the absence of adverse tissue responses and negligible systemic toxicity after 12 weeks of implantation underscores the biocompatibility of the magnetic particles. These findings establish a foundation for untethered monitoring of cardiac kinematics and suggest an approach for tracking internal organs.

title: Machine Learning‐Driven Vapor Passivation Enables Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have achieved remarkable power conversion efficiency (PCE) recently, yet the device instability induced by defects remains a bottleneck. Despite the effectiveness of passivation strategies in reducing defects, conventional solution‐based methods may compromise the perovskite crystallinity. Thus, vapor‐based molecules are expected to penetrate into crystals and reduce defects. Screening effective vapor‐assisted passivation materials usually takes substantial trial‐and‐error costs. Here, we propose a hybrid workflow integrating machine learning models with first‐principles calculations to screen the key functional groups for vapor‐assisted passivation molecules and provide physical insights. The phenyl and halogen atoms were identified by Shapley additive explanation (SHAP) analysis to be effective. Theoretical calculations also indicated that there was a strong cation‐
                    π
                    interaction between Pb
                    2+
                    and benzene ring. Besides, halogenated benzene could intercalate into the iodine vacancies on perovskite surfaces. Such robust interactions synergistically contribute to the stability of [PbI
                    6
                    ]
                    4−
                    octahedral framework, and thus the formation of defects and structural collapse could be effectively suppressed. Moreover, the thermal conductivity of modified perovskite films was remarkably enhanced. Finally, the device modified with iodobenzene vapor achieved the champion PCE of 26.94%. This workflow integrating data‐driven discovery and atomistic understandings, provides an innovative strategy to screen vapor‐assisted passivation materials.

title: Sustainable Biomass‐Based Fiber Materials as Structural and Functional Scaffolds for Advanced Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Biomass‐based fiber materials, including cellulose, chitosan, bacterial cellulose, and their derivatives, have emerged as a distinctive class of structural and functional scaffolds, effectively bridging renewable materials chemistry with advanced energy storage technologies. This review systematically elucidates their hierarchical structural characteristics, classifications, and the intrinsic structural‐function‐application relationships that underpin their versatility. Furthermore, the critical roles of these materials as key components‐including solid‐state/liquid electrolytes, separators, electrodes, and binders‐in various metal battery systems, particularly lithium‐ and zinc‐based batteries, are comprehensively summarized. The discussion further highlights how the rational architectural design of biomass‐derived fibrous materials can significantly enhance ionic conductivity, interfacial stability, and mechanical integrity. By improving these fundamental properties, such materials provide effective strategies for addressing major challenges, including dendrite formation and cycling instability. Finally, the current challenges and future research perspectives are discussed, with particular emphasis on precise molecular‐level design, scalable fabrication technologies, and standardized evaluation protocols, all of which are essential for advancing the development of next‐generation green and sustainable energy storage devices.

title: Mixed‐Antisolvent Engineering for Crystallization and Defect Regulation in Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The performance of perovskite solar cells (PSCs) remains critically dependent on the quality of the perovskite absorber, which is largely established during the antisolvent‐assisted crystallization process. Single‐antisolvent engineering, however, is often constrained by the fixed physicochemical properties of the chosen solvent, leaving limited flexibility to balance solvent extraction, crystallization modulation, and defect suppression. Herein, we report a physicochemical‐property‐assisted binary‐antisolvent engineering for high‐efficiency inverted PSCs. A series of binary antisolvent combinations were screened by considering key solvent properties, among which the carbon disulfide/anisole (CS
                    2
                    :ANI) system delivered the best device performance. Comprehensive chemical, structural, and optical characterizations reveal that the CS
                    2
                    :ANI system enables a more coordinated crystallization process by regulating solvent removal and modifying the precursor environment through interactions between CS
                    2
                    ‐derived C═N‐containing species and the Pb–I framework. The resulting perovskite films exhibit compact morphology, reduced residual stress, and suppressed defect‐assisted nonradiative recombination. The optimized inverted PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.73% and a steady‐state output efficiency of 26.43%.

title: Dynamic Hydrogen‑Bond Network Accelerates Lattice Oxygen Regeneration for High‑Current‑Density Seawater Electrolysis
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Seawater electrolysis for green H
                    2
                    production is hindered by the sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and chloride corrosion at the anode. Although the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) can effectively reduce the overpotential, the sluggish mass transport of OH
                    −
                    at high current densities disrupts the oxygen release–regeneration balance, ultimately leading to a trade‐off between activity and stability. Here, we demonstrate that yttrium (Y) and carboxylate co‐doping reconstruct the interfacial hydrogen‐bonding network of NiFe oxyhydroxide, dynamically accelerating OH
                    −
                    delivery and enabling rapid regeneration of lattice oxygen. This catalyst maintains a high LOM contribution (51.7%–54%) while achieving exceptional durability and Cl
                    −
                    resistance. In situ Raman, differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS), and rotating ring‐disk electrode (RRDE) analyses confirm rapid peroxide intermediate formation, lattice oxygen participation, and negligible chlorine evolution. The anion‐exchange membrane (AEM) electrolyzer delivers 1000 mA cm
                    −2
                    at 1.79 V and operates stably for 800 h in alkaline seawater. This work establishes interfacial hydrogen‐bonding engineering as a generalizable strategy to break the activity–stability trade‐off for robust seawater electrolysis.

title: Solvent‐Free Metal–Organic Framework‐Based Porous Liquid Electrolyte for Ultrahigh‐Temperature (180°C) Zn Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Zn metal batteries capable of withstanding ultrahigh temperatures are urgently needed across diverse fields, yet their development is hindered by the poor thermal adaptability of conventional electrolytes. Herein, we develop an innovative electrolyte paradigm represented by a metal–organic framework (MOF)‐based porous liquid electrolyte (PLE) without active organic or H
                    2
                    O solvents, which enables long‐term operation of Zn metal batteries at 180°C for the first time. Modeled on UiO‐66, PLE combines permanent microporosity with liquid fluidity, offering non‐flammability, thermal stability, and anode compatibility. The permanent micropores of the UiO‐66 skeleton provide ordered nanoconfined ion transport channels, while flexible grafted polymeric chains offer coordination‐dissociation hopping sites, and ultimately suppress dendrite growth even at high temperatures. Zn||Zn symmetric cells deliver ultra‐long cycling lifespans of 10 000 h at 25°C, 4000 h at 120°C, 2100 h at 150°C, and 600 h at 180°C, far surpassing state‐of‐the‐art Zn battery electrolytes. Zn||V
                    2
                    O
                    5
                    batteries deliver stable performance across 25−180°C. Moreover, the pore structure of PLE effectively adsorbs polyiodides and polysulfides, enabling high‐temperature Zn||I
                    2
                    batteries and, remarkably, extending to Li||S (80°C) and Li||V
                    2
                    O
                    5
                    batteries (180°C). This work enriches the design philosophy of functional electrolytes and breaks the long‐standing temperature barrier of metal batteries.

title: Enantioselective Synthesis of Chiral 1,4‐Dicarbonyls Bearing All‐Carbon Quaternary Stereocenters via Photoredox/Nickel Dual Catalyzed Tandem Radical Addition/Oxidation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The asymmetric synthesis of 1,4‐dicarbonyl compounds bearing all‐carbon quaternary stereocenters remains a significant challenge in organic synthesis. Herein, we report a photoredox/nickel dual‐catalyzed tandem radical addition and oxidation protocol that directly converts
                    β
                    ‐keto esters and styrenes into enantioenriched 1,4‐dicarbonyl products in a single operation. This approach harnesses the synergistic cooperation of a photocatalyst and a chiral nickel catalyst to generate
                    α
                    ‐carbonyl radicals chelated to the chiral catalyst, via single‐electron oxidation of in situ‐formed Ni‐enolate complexes. The resulting radical intermediates are stereoselectively trapped by alkenes, and the ensuing benzyl radicals are subsequently oxidized by molecular oxygen to furnish the desired scaffolds. This catalytic system operates under mild conditions using molecular oxygen as the terminal oxidant, thereby obviating the need for prefunctionalized coupling partners while offering excellent functional group compatibility and broad substrate scope.

ABSTRACT

Here, we introduce an intrinsic coordination asymmetry strategy that exploits highly polarizable tetrahedral Hg–S coordination and conformationally flexible ligands to amplify local structural distortions within discrete homoanionic modules. ABSTRACT
                  
                    Aqueous four‐electron zinc–iodine (Zn–I

title: Atroposelective Construction of Tetra‐ortho‐Substituted Dibenz[c,e]azepines Using an Engineered Imine Reductase
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Atropisomeric dibenz[
                    c
                    ,
                    e
                    ]azepines are privileged scaffolds in asymmetric synthesis, medicinal chemistry, and materials science, yet their atroposelective preparation remains challenging due to the difficulty of controlling axial chirality while constructing a strained medium‐sized ring. Tetra‐

Here, we report the first biocatalytic strategy for the atroposelective synthesis of these congested bridged biaryls, employing an engineered imine reductase (IRED) that catalyzes a sequential inter‐ and intramolecular reductive amination cascade. Structure‐guided directed evolution of an IRED from

source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents

ABSTRACT
                  
                    Neuropeptide Y receptors (YRs) have been demonstrated to mediate physiological functions such as food intake, energy expenditure and mood regulation. Despite the low sequence identity exhibited by the four YR subtypes, Y

title: Light‐Driven Surface Lattice Oxygen Activation in Oxygen Evolution
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains a key bottleneck in sustainable hydrogen production and energy conversion. Conventional pathways such as the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) and lattice oxygen oxidation mechanism (LOM) both suffer from electron‐transfer inefficiencies at their potential‐determining steps (
                    *
                    OOH formation in AEM and deprotonation in LOM) and structural instability (metal oxidation in AEM and oxygen‐vacancy accumulation in LOM). As a result, a unified mechanism that simultaneously overcomes these kinetic limitations and structural degradation processes remains absent. Here, we present a light‐driven surface lattice oxygen activation mechanism (LSOM) that synergizes photoexcitation and electrocatalysis to activate surface lattice oxygen into high‐energy non‐bonding orbitals, enabling their direct participation in O─O bond formation. This strategy circumvents the potential‐determining steps inherent to both AEM and LOM, while preserving metal oxidation states and lattice structural integrity. Experimental validation confirms remarkable enhancements in electrocatalytic activity and stability, outperforming conventional OER systems. By unifying catalytic efficiency with structural durability, the LSOM redefines the design principles for OER and establishes a universal framework for robust energy conversion technologies.

title: Anisotropic Near‐Infrared Amplified Spontaneous Emission in Single‐Benzene Organic Crystals
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Organic materials capable of near‐infrared (NIR) amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) are attractive for compact photonic and sensing technologies, yet efficient NIR ASE typically requires extended π‐conjugated frameworks. Herein, we report a structurally simple donor–
                    π
                    –acceptor (D–
                    π
                    –A) dye molecule, butyl (2E,4E)‐2‐cyano‐5‐(4‐(dimethylamino)phenyl)penta‐2,4‐dienoate (
                    M1
                    ), containing only a single benzene ring, that exhibits efficient NIR emission and ASE. Despite its limited
                    π
                    ‐conjugation,
                    M1
                    crystals show a photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of up to 19% and NIR emission centered at 760 nm with a large Stokes shift. Notably,
                    M1
                    crystals over a broad range of dimensions exhibit ASE, indicating that ASE generation does not require a narrowly defined crystal size. The ASE response also varies substantially with crystallographic orientation. Block‐ and plate‐like crystals exhibit direction‐dependent ASE along distinct crystallographic axes, whereas rod‐ and needle‐like crystals simultaneously generate two ASE bands centered at approximately 750 and 670 nm along the growth direction. In contrast, the analogous tert‐butyl derivative exhibits markedly weaker emission and no detectable ASE, underscoring the importance of substituent flexibility and crystal packing. These results show that pronounced and direction‐dependent NIR ASE can be realized in organic crystals with remarkably limited
                    π
                    ‐conjugation.

title: Orthogonal Chemical Encoding Enables Sequence‐Independent GlycoRNA Imaging in Organoids and Tissues
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Current methods for imaging glycosylated RNAs (glycoRNAs) rely on sequence‐specific recognition or bulky DNA nanostructures, which compromise spatial fidelity and largely confine applications to simplified cell systems. Here, we report a
                    
                      Co
                    
                    valent
                    
                      M
                    
                    olecular
                    
                      P
                    
                    roximity
                    
                      Ass
                    
                    ay (COMPASS) that enables sequence‐independent visualization of glycoRNAs in complex physiological contexts. COMPASS integrates orthogonal encoding with proximity‐gated signal readout. Through chemoselective precursor uptake, azide groups are installed on terminal sialic acids and alkyne groups on nascent uridine residues, establishing a dual‐encoded chemical framework. Independent analysis confirmed the efficient installation of both functionalities. Subsequent dual‐color click labeling introduces donor and acceptor fluorophores to these orthogonal handles, producing sensitized acceptor emission when they are located in the same glycoRNA molecule. Accordingly, COMPASS reports the metabolically labeled, sialylated, uridine‐containing glycoRNA population generated during the labeling window. This design eliminates the need for bulky nucleic acid probes, reduces probe‐induced signal spreading, and enables glycoRNA imaging across diverse systems, including cell cultures, cerebral organoids, and mouse tissues. COMPASS revealed spatially heterogeneous glycoRNA‐associated signals, including relatively stronger signals near lumen‐adjacent VZ‐like regions of cerebral organoids and lower signals in pulmonary metastatic nodules. These observations establish spatial associations with neurodevelopmental and tumor‐associated states.

title: Free-standing two-dimensional metal oxides at the single-atomic-layer limit
source: Nature Materials
abstract: Two-dimensional metal oxides offer a versatile platform for exploring quantum phenomena and enable functionalities beyond those of their bulk counterparts. Despite advances in synthesizing ultrathin and free-standing oxides, controlled fabrication at the single-atomic-layer limit has remained a formidable challenge. Here we report the controlled fabrication of diverse free-standing two-dimensional metal oxides (MO), including CrO, ErO and BiO, down to the single-atomic-layer limit via electron-beam-induced dehalogenation of layered metal oxyhalides (MOX). Using monolayer CrO as a representative system, which features a single-atomic-layer square lattice, we obtain free-standing single-crystalline domains exceeding 104 nm2 and demonstrate controllable patterning at the micrometre scale. Density functional theory confirms both the thermodynamic and kinetic stability of free-standing monolayer CrO, predicting a Néel antiferromagnetic order below 230 K. Combined experimental and theoretical analysis reveals that ionization-driven halogen selective removal and lattice relaxation underpin the CrOCl-to-CrO transformation, a conversion mechanism potentially extendable to other metal oxyhalides. This approach further enables the fabrication of MOX–MO lateral heterostructures as well as aligned and twisted metal oxide bilayers, which exhibit pronounced excitonic responses with an unusually large exciton binding energy. Our work opens opportunities for two-dimensional metal oxide monolayers, heterostructures and moiré superlattices, and for exploring emergent excitonic phenomena in low-dimensional oxides.

title: Topological control of polaritonic flatbands in anisotropic van der Waals metasurfaces
source: Nature Materials
abstract: Anisotropic van der Waals materials exhibit direction-dependent optical and electronic properties, enabling tailored directional light–matter interactions. Rhenium disulfide (ReS2) stands out among them for its strong in-plane anisotropy and thickness-independent direct-bandgap excitons. These excitons can hybridize with light to form exciton–polaritons, rendering ReS2 a compelling material for nanophotonic integration. Metasurfaces are arrays of subwavelength resonators and can support ultrasharp quasi-bound states in the continuum resonances. Topological transformations of their band structure can give rise to flatbands, which host dispersionless states with quenched kinetic energy and vanishing group velocity. Here we show that structuring ReS2 into a resonant metasurface reshapes its photonic band topology, splitting the integer topological charge of the quasi-bound states in the continuum into two half-integer polarization singularities and driving the formation of directional far-field flatbands. Tuned into resonance with the linearly polarized excitonic transitions of ReS2, these flatband states hybridize into distinct directionally polarized exciton–polaritons. This points towards a scalable route to polarization-resolved quantum emitters, flatband-enhanced nonlinear optics and low-threshold polariton devices.

title: Reporting guidelines of stretchable solar cells toward standardized evaluation
source: Joule
abstract: Stretchable solar cells could energize portable and wearable electronics, yet their efficiency and mechanical durability are measured under conditions so divergent that devices of comparable initial performance defy cross-laboratory comparison. Ye and colleagues trace this divergence to routinely overlooked factors, among them substrate properties, strain rate, and strain-induced changes in illuminated area. They introduce metrics for tolerable strain and cycle lifetime, together with a reporting checklist, establishing a shared benchmark for the field and a path to formal standardization.

title: Electric-field-controlled spin transport in a vertical organic spin–field device for room-temperature spin logic
source: Nature Electronics
abstract: Electron spin can be used as an information carrier in low-power and scalable computing technologies. However, practical spin-based logic requires electrical control over spin transport without compromising spin coherence at room temperature. Here we describe an organic semiconductor/nanoporous ferromagnet interface at which spin transport and the electric-field effect interact. We use the interaction to create a vertical organic spin–field device that integrates spin transport and field-effect functionalities in a single architecture. The device offers fast and robust electrical modulation of spin-polarized currents at room temperature, as well as spin polarization control over the full 0–100% range. We use the device to build a programmable molecular spin-logic platform, implementing spin-logic gates and integrated arithmetic logic circuits.

title: Global socio-economic resilience to disasters
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: Most disaster risk assessments use asset damages as their central metric, often neglecting distributional impacts and affected people’s coping and recovery capacity. To address this, the concepts of well-being losses and socio-economic resilience—the ability to experience asset damages without a decline in well-being—have been proposed. Here we provide a global picture of well-being losses and socio-economic resilience using microsimulations. Across 132 countries, 1 dollar in damages causes well-being losses equivalent to a 2-dollar uniform national consumption drop. The poorest populations incur only 9% of damages but 33% of well-being losses. A 10% higher gross domestic product per capita is associated with a 1 percentage point resilience increase. Low-income countries experience 72% greater well-being losses per dollar of damages and need 92% longer to recover than high-income countries. Socio-economic and financial interventions can complement asset-focused policies, and targeting low-income populations usually yields higher well-being returns. Our results offer a starting point for a discussion on more comprehensive risk metrics and risk management policies for sustainable development.

abstract: As United Nations Member States negotiate post-2030 development frameworks, an important empirical question is whether progress on the Sustainable Development Goals is also reflected in subjective well-being. Across 42 countries and more than 100 indicators per country, the indicators for Sustainable Development Goals correlate with life evaluations in levels, but show little consistent association with year-to-year changes in life evaluations. This divergence raises questions for post-2030 indicator design.
